### (e) Financing for Specific Segments

#### (i) 300 Billion Yuan Affordable Housing Relending Facility (保障性住房再贷款)

**Establishment:** On May 17, 2024, the PBOC announced a 300 billion yuan affordable housing relending facility. Key parameters:
- Size: 300 billion yuan
- Interest rate: 1.75%
- Term: 1 year, renewable up to 4 times
- Distributed to 21 national banks including CDB, policy banks, state-owned commercial banks, postal savings, and joint-stock banks [7][8][9][10]
- Initially, the PBOC would provide relending equal to 60% of loan principal, potentially driving 500 billion yuan in bank lending [7][8]
- On September 24, 2024, PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng announced the PBOC's funding share was raised from 60% to 100%, meaning for every 100 yuan lent by commercial banks, the PBOC now provides 100 yuan in low-cost funds to accelerate inventory reduction [7]

**Implementation progress:**
- Over 100 cities have established acquisition working groups and selected acquisition entities; 70+ cities have publicly released housing source solicitation announcements [6]
- By January 2025, cities including Chongqing, Wuhan, Zhengzhou, Changchun, and Jinhua had completed existing housing acquisition projects, collecting over 10,000 units of affordable housing [6][7]
- Examples: CDB Suzhou Branch issued 1.1 billion yuan in syndicated loans to support purchase of unsold developer housing for resale on a "break-even with small profit" principle [7]; ICBC Chongqing Branch loaned to Jiayu Company for 1,000+ rental apartments now fully leased [7]; Hefei Anju Group acquired 5,733 units (589,000 sqm) of existing commercial housing [7]

**Policy outlook:** The relending facility had significant unused capacity within its 300 billion yuan quota as of end-2024, meaning more acquisition projects would receive funding [6]. The Central Economic Work Conference (December 2024) proposed "advancing the disposal of existing commercial housing" [6].

#### (ii) Special Bonds (专项债) for Land Purchase and Housing Inventory Reduction

**2025 Government Work Report:** Allocated 4.4 trillion yuan in local government special bonds (up 500 billion yuan from prior year), focused on "investment construction, land purchase and acquisition of existing commercial housing, and resolving government overdue debts to enterprises" [8][13][14].

**Policy timeline:**
- October 12, 2024: Ministry of Finance announced that special bond funds could be used for land reserves and purchasing existing housing stock [7]
- November 2024: Ministry of Natural Resources issued notice on using special bonds to recover idle land [8]
- December 2024: State Council issued "Opinions on Optimizing and Improving Local Government Special Bond Management Mechanism" [8]
- January 10, 2025: Finance Ministry's Lin Zechang confirmed that within the 2025 new special bond quota, local governments can arrange for these two purposes; policy effects will gradually materialize in 2025 [7][11]
- March 11, 2025: Ministry of Natural Resources and Ministry of Finance jointly issued notice on using special bonds for land reserves [8]

**Land reserve (土地收储) implementation:**
- By July 25, 2025, 45 special bonds for land reserves totaling 239.3 billion yuan across 937 projects had been issued (12.33% of all special bonds) [6]
- By October 24, 2025, provinces announced proposed acquisitions exceeding 620 billion yuan with ~216 billion actually issued [6]
- Q3 2025 issuance accelerated to monthly average 32.5 billion yuan, up 49% from Q2 [6]
- Provincial examples: Guangdong issued 307.1859 billion yuan for 86 projects across 19 cities (February 24, 2025) [8]; Hunan issued 9.4 billion yuan (April 8); Fujian 14.96 billion (May 8); Zhejiang 19.19 billion across three tranches covering 70 projects in 10 cities [6]
- Over 5,500 parcels of idle land were slated for repurchase via special bonds (nearly 300 million sqm, 750+ billion yuan) [23]

**Acquisition of existing commercial housing for affordable housing:**
- On May 13, 2025, Zhejiang Province became the first in China to use special bonds to acquire existing commercial housing, with over 1.6 billion yuan allocated for this purpose — a functional breakthrough broadening beyond the previous financial tool (affordable housing relending loans) to now include fiscal tools (special bonds) [9][12]
- Zhejiang's special bonds covered 8 residential projects in Huzhou, Wenzhou, and Jiaxing, primarily to be converted into affordable rental housing [9][12]
- Inventory destocking cycles for new residential housing in 2025 were 42, 22, and 23 months for Huzhou, Wenzhou, and Jiaxing respectively [9][12]
- Sichuan's bond list also included 168 million yuan for repurchasing existing commercial housing in Nanchong for affordable housing [9][12]

**Expert analysis:**
- Yan Yuejin (严跃进): "This year, special bonds as an important fiscal tool for local governments to acquire idle land have played a positive role in revitalizing idle land and accelerating land risk resolution" [6]
- Chen Wenjing (陈文静): "In Q3, the issuance of special bonds for acquiring idle land accelerated, with monthly average issuance of 32.5 billion yuan, up about 49% from Q2" [6]
- China Banking Research Institute's Ye Yindan: "Special bond land purchases can cut land inventory from the source, curb land price decline trends, avoid developers dumping land to raise funds for delivery guarantees, and accelerate the revitalization and utilization of idle land" [8]

#### (iii) 2025 Fiscal Package — 4 Trillion Yuan Local Special Bonds, 1.3 Trillion Yuan Ultra-long-term Special Treasury Bonds

The 2025 Government Work Report called for a "more proactive" fiscal policy with total new government debt reaching 11.86 trillion yuan, a 2.9 trillion yuan increase over the previous year [13]. Key provisions:
- Issuance of 1.3 trillion yuan in ultra-long-term special treasury bonds (up 300 billion yuan from last year), with increased support for both "两重" (major national strategies and security building) and "两新" (two new initiatives) [13]
- A 500 billion yuan special treasury bond issuance to support capital replenishment for major state-owned commercial banks [13]
- Arrangement of 4.4 trillion yuan in local government special bonds (up 500 billion yuan) [13][14]
- Implementation of the previously approved 2 trillion yuan annual local government debt swap quota for replacing implicit (hidden) debt [13]
- The November 2024 National People's Congress decision increased local government debt limits by 6 trillion yuan for implicit debt swaps (2 trillion yuan annually from 2024-2026), plus an additional 800 billion yuan annually from new local special bonds for five consecutive years for debt resolution (4 trillion yuan total), providing up to 10 trillion yuan in local debt resolution resources [13]

**2026 Outlook:** January 5, 2026, Shandong Province issued 72.381 billion yuan in local government bonds, making it the first province to issue local government bonds in 2026 [1]. The Central Economic Work Conference (December 10-11, 2025) called for "continuing more proactive fiscal policies" [1]. Wang Yunjin, Chief Financial Researcher at Guangqi Chief Industry Research Institute, forecasts: special local government bond quota of 4.8 trillion yuan for 2026 (up 400 billion yuan from 2025), new total government debt exceeding 13 trillion yuan, broad fiscal deficit ratio rising to ~8.8%, and 2.8 trillion yuan in debt resolution quota [1]. The Ministry of Finance established a new Debt Management Department in November 2025 [1].

#### (iv) Urban Village Renovation (城中村改造) Financing

**CDB Data (as of end of August 2025):**
Since the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-2025), the China Development Bank has:
- Disbursed 978.1 billion yuan in urban village renovation special loans, supporting 816 projects, helping build/raise 1.769 million resettlement houses, benefiting 942,000 urban village households [15][16]
- Disbursed 4.8 billion yuan in affordable housing loans, supporting 74 projects, helping build/raise 62,000 affordable housing units [15][16]
- Disbursed 40.7 billion yuan in "peace-emergency dual-use" (平急两用) public infrastructure loans, supporting 180 projects [15][16]

The CDB established "two-level working groups (headquarters and branch) with working mechanisms to strengthen coordination, deepen connections with ministries and local governments, enhance credit resource guarantees, and establish fast-track approval channels to fully meet the financing needs of the 'three major projects'" [15][16].

**2025 Expansion:**
- On January 3, 2025, a State Council executive meeting studied urban renewal work and called for accelerating renovation of old residential communities, neighborhoods, factory areas, and urban villages [18]
- In 2024, urban village renovation expanded to over 300 cities, with 1,790 projects implemented [18]
- For 2025, MOHURD intensified urban village and dilapidated housing renovation, promoting monetized resettlement, and continued to expand renovation scale beyond the new 1 million units target to stabilize the property market [18]
- Data shows that in just 35 major cities, 1.7 million units of urban villages need renovation [18]
- Qualified urban village renovation projects can receive policy support including local government special bond support, special loans from development/policy financial institutions, tax incentives, and commercial bank loans [18]

**Expert estimates:** Guosen Securities chief economist Xia Lei estimated that the 1 million-unit monetized resettlement could drive 200 million square meters of commercial housing sales, and reasonable land planning adjustments could drive approximately 500 billion yuan in on-site construction investment [18].

**Background:** The State Council issued the "Guidance on Actively and Steadily Promoting Urban Village Redevelopment in Super Large Cities" in July 2023 [19]. Redevelopment proceeds through three modes: demolition and reconstruction, regular renovation/upgrades, and a combination of both [19]. Professor Ye Yumin (Renmin University) noted that urban villages face issues including land use inefficiency, public health and safety hazards, poor infrastructure, and "housing poverty." The average demolition/reconstruction cycle takes about 10 years [19].

### (f) Indirect Financing Trends — Capital Markets, Developer Bond Issuance, Equity Financing, and Insurance/Pension Fund Investment

#### Developer Bond Issuance

**2025 Data:**
Real estate enterprise bond financing totaled 5,967.2 billion yuan in 2025, up 5.6% year-on-year [21]. Key characteristics:
- Credit bonds remained the absolute mainstay, accounting for 57.5% of total financing (3,428.7 billion yuan, down 0.6% YoY) [21]
- ABS (asset-backed securities) financing totaled 2,377 billion yuan, up 11.2% YoY, accounting for 39.8% of total financing [21]
- Overseas bonds recovered from a low base, reaching 16.15 billion yuan (up 141% YoY) but still only 2.7% of total financing [21]
- Credit bond issuers were predominantly central state-owned enterprises (央企) and local state-owned enterprises (地方国企), accounting for 92% of issuance, up 1 percentage point from 2024 [21]
- Major developers like Poly Developments, China Resources Land, China Merchants Shekou, and China Overseas each issued over 100 billion yuan [21]
- Poly Developments successfully issued a record 85 billion yuan directional convertible bond in May 2025, "the largest real estate refinancing project since the 2022 policy" [21]
- The average bond interest rate fell significantly to 2.69% (down 0.26 pp), driven by interest rate cuts and changes in issuer/product structure. Credit bonds averaged 2.48% (down 0.38 pp), overseas bonds averaged 6.06% (up 0.84 pp), and ABS averaged 2.76% (down 0.25 pp) [21]
- The average issuance term for credit bonds extended to 3.72 years, and for ABS to 12.65 years [21]
- CMBS/CMBN and quasi-REITs were the main ABS types, with CMBS/CMBN share rising rapidly [21]

**For January-November 2025:** Total bond financing reached 550.28 billion yuan, up 10.5% year-on-year [13]. In November 2025, real estate bond financing totaled 62.04 billion yuan, up 28.5% year-on-year [13].

**Private developer overseas bond issuance:**
After overseas bond windows were essentially closed to private developers since 2024, Greentown issued $500 million overseas bonds in February 2025 at 8.45% coupon, and Seazen issued $300 million in June 2025 at 11.88% coupon — marking the reopening of overseas financing for private developers [22]. Both issuances were primarily for refinancing existing overseas debt, not for new investment [22].

Private developer domestic credit bond issuance in 2025 (Jan-May) remained limited to healthy brands: Meidi Real Estate (RMB 4.5bn at 3.35%), Binjiang (RMB 1.7bn at 3.76%), New Hope (RMB 1.21bn at 3.23%) [22].

Total overseas debt outstanding for developers: RMB 125.04 billion in 2025, RMB 142.7 billion in 2026, RMB 375.73 billion from 2027 onward (total RMB 643.47 billion as of end-May data) [22].

#### Insurance and Pension Fund Investment in Rental Housing

Insurance capital (险资) has been increasingly investing in "rent-collecting" assets (收租型资产) such as commercial real estate, office buildings, and long-term rental housing [16].

**Key investment examples:**
- 华夏凯德商业REIT listed on September 29, 2025, with 财信人寿 participating as the largest external investor (approximately 50 million yuan). The REIT's underlying assets include the 长沙凯德广场雨花亭 project (75,000 sqm, ~97% occupancy) [16]
- Insurance companies including 中国人寿, 太平洋人寿, 平安人寿, and 建信人寿 announced over ten large real estate investments in 2025, totaling tens of billions of yuan — significantly more than the same period last year, targeting commercial offices and logistics real estate [16]
- A 4.5 billion yuan 天津家寓股权投资基金 was launched by 大家投控 with participants including 大家人寿, 友邦人寿, 中宏人寿, and 复星保德信人寿 — described as "the insurance industry's first value-add long-term rental housing fund, focused on Beijing and Shanghai affordable rental housing" [16]
- 友邦人寿 acquired 上海松江柚米社区 (2,200+ affordable rental units) in July 2025 [16]
- 新华保险, 大家人寿, and 万科 established the 万新金石基金 to acquire 厦门泊寓院儿·海湾社区 (7,700+ units) [16]

**Policy support:** This includes the 2022 CBIRC/MOHURD guidance on bank and insurance institution support for affordable rental housing, and 2024 PBOC/financial regulator guidance on financial support for the rental housing market [16].

**Market context:** JLL data shows rental yields on Tier-1 city commercial real estate remain at 5.5%-6.5%, with JLL China investment head Pang Shudong (庞树东) noting the yield differential vs. 10-year government bonds makes such assets attractive [16]. Insurance funds are described as "careful rent collectors" seeking stable cash-flow assets amid declining fixed-income yields, with the 募投管退 (raise-invest-manage-exit) cycle now more complete thanks to public REITs as an exit channel [16].

**Cross-sector products:** 太保资产—新黄浦筑梦城保租房持有型不动产资产支持专项计划 was issued in H1 2026, over 11 billion yuan [20]. Multi-tier REITs market includes public REITs, inter-institutional REITs (机构间REITs, 2025 issuance exceeding 530 billion yuan), and quasi-REITs (类REITs, 2025 issuance exceeding 900 billion yuan) [20].

### (g) Green/Sustainable Finance for Real Estate

#### Green Credit (绿色信贷)

As of end-2025, China's domestic and foreign currency green loan balance reached 44.77 trillion yuan, with a full-year increase of 7.72 trillion yuan, achieving year-on-year growth of over 20% [22].

**Major bank green loan balances (2025 data):**
- ICBC: green loan balance exceeded 6.7 trillion yuan, with new additions of over 1 trillion yuan [20]
- Agricultural Bank of China: green loan balance of 5.93 trillion yuan; issued 66 billion yuan in green financial bonds (largest among peers) [20]
- Bank of China: green loan balance of 4.96 trillion yuan, up 27.83% year-over-year [20]
- SPDB: green loan balance of 707.374 billion yuan, up 23.95% [20]
- Huaxia Bank: green finance balance of 531.352 billion yuan, up 31.42% [20]

#### Green Bonds (绿色债券)

**Market size:** In 2025, China's domestic green bond market issued 645 new bonds totaling approximately 10,778.83 billion yuan, breaking through the trillion-yuan annual level for the first time. This represented a 35.22% increase in quantity and a 58.18% increase in scale compared to 2024 [21]. From 2016 to end-2025, cumulative domestic green bond issuance reached approximately 5.23 trillion yuan, accounting for about 3.23% of all credit bonds [21].

**China's green bond market has risen to become the world's largest** [24]. From 2016 to 2024, green bond issuance in China grew from 201.8 billion yuan to 683.3 billion yuan, an annual average growth of 16.5%. Issuers grew from 35 to 249, and the number of bonds issued grew ninefold. By the end of 2024, there were 1,868 outstanding green bonds totaling 2.2 trillion yuan; when including non-labeled bonds actually invested in green areas, the "green-invested" bond market exceeds 6 trillion yuan [24].

**Investment allocation:** Top three areas are clean energy, green infrastructure upgrades, and energy conservation, accounting for 3.6 trillion yuan (83% of total green bond funds) [24]. Each 100 million yuan of green bonds supports reduction of 4,583 tons of CO2 equivalent, with an estimated total emission reduction of 520 million tons of CO2 equivalent [24].

**Cost advantages:** Green bonds have shown increasing issuance cost advantages. In 2021, after the PBOC's policy expanded performance assessment to include green bonds, green bond issuance costs fell notably — 10.1 BP lower than ordinary bonds. Cost advantages were 5.3 BP in 2023 and 11.1 BP in 2024. Bonds with fully disclosed environmental benefit information had average financing costs 6.5 BP lower than those with incomplete disclosure [24].

**Policy framework:** The July 2025 "Green Financial Support Project Catalogue (2025 Edition)" updated the green project classification system, strengthening support for new energy, energy storage, grid upgrades, and green manufacturing, and added green trade and green consumption [21][22]. The 2023 Central Financial Work Conference designated green finance as one of the "five major articles" for building a financial powerhouse [24].

**Innovative green bond types:**
- Carbon neutrality bonds: 151 bonds issued in 2025 (approximately 1,514.93 billion yuan), cumulative 740 bonds totaling about 1 trillion yuan [21]
- Transition bonds: 80 bonds issued in 2025 (approximately 437.42 billion yuan), including sustainability-linked bonds (38 bonds, 229 billion yuan), low-carbon transition-linked bonds (35 bonds, 179 billion yuan), and low-carbon transition bonds (7 bonds, 29.1 billion yuan) [21]
- Rural revitalization bonds: 105 bonds (approximately 600 billion yuan) [21]
- Sci-tech innovation corporate bonds: 97 bonds (quantity up 506.25% year-on-year) [21]

#### Green Finance for Real Estate and Green Buildings

The PBOC, NFRA, and CSRC jointly issued the "Green Financial Support Project Catalogue (2025 Edition)" which covers green buildings and green infrastructure as eligible categories [21][22]. The China Green Bond White Paper notes that investment covers all six categories of the Green Bond Support Project Catalogue, with green infrastructure upgrades being the second-largest category [24].

**ESG integration in REITs:**
The Shenzhen Securities Regulatory Bureau guided industry discussions on "Infrastructure REITs Trial ESG Evaluation" in March 2025, with experts introducing international ESG evaluation development history and domestic ESG regulatory requirements evolution, and making recommendations on REITs ESG information disclosure standards and incorporating ESG ratings into issuance and ongoing management [19].

Liu Feng (刘锋), Chief Economist at the Central University of Finance and Economy's Green Finance International Research Institute, noted that "Chinese banking's ESG practice has shifted from passive compliance to active governance, with ESG becoming a risk management tool moving 'from compliance requirements to value creation'" [20]. He recommended converting ESG from a "cost item" to a "risk mitigation tool," obtaining differentiated pricing space through ESG-linked products, developing green-related intermediary businesses, and seeking excess return opportunities in transition finance [20].

**2025 Green Finance Milestones:**
- The Ministry of Finance issued the first offshore green sovereign bond on the London Stock Exchange (60 billion yuan, 3-year and 5-year tranches, rates 1.88% and 1.93%, oversubscribed 6.9 times) [22]
- The State Administration of Foreign Exchange launched green foreign debt pilot programs in 16 cities [22]
- Nine ministries including the Ministry of Finance issued climate disclosure standards requiring industry-level disclosure of total financed emissions [22]
- Transition finance implementation guides were published in Guangdong, Shanghai, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang for building materials, paper, textiles, and other industries [22]

### Summary of Current Situation as of 2026 and Projections to 2035

**Current Situation (2026):**
- 5-year LPR at 3.50% (record low), RRR at ~6.2%, policy rate (7-day reverse repo) at 1.4%
- Whitelist mechanism: over 7 trillion yuan in approved loans, supporting nearly 20 million housing units
- REITs: 86 listed products, 210+ billion yuan scale, with commercial REITs pilot newly launched
- HPF: 10.9 trillion yuan in balance, coverage expanding to 176 million contributors, with major reform pushed to central policy agenda
- Fiscal: 4.4 trillion yuan in special bonds (2025), with special bonds newly allowed for land reserves and housing inventory acquisition
- Urban village renovation: 978.1 billion yuan in CDB special loans since 2021
- Green finance: 44.77 trillion yuan in green loans, 10.78 trillion yuan in green bonds (2025)
- Bond financing: 5,967.2 billion yuan (2025), up 5.6% YoY, average rate 2.69%
- Insurance capital: increasingly active in rental housing and commercial real estate investment

**Projections to 2035:**
- **Monetary policy:** Continued loose stance expected; further rate cuts and RRR cuts anticipated; LPR expected to remain at 3.5% or potentially lower through 2027 per econometric models [14]; additional easing measures likely including new policy financial instruments
- **REITs:** Market expected to reach trillion-yuan scale; full asset class coverage (commercial real estate, data centers, cultural tourism, pension); normalized issuance with "primary + expansion" dual-driver model; deepened REITs legislation and tax system; expanded long-term capital participation
- **Whitelist mechanism:** Transitioning from emergency support to routine financing system; integrated into new real estate development model framework
- **HPF reform:** Transformation from single home-purchase tool to full life-cycle housing consumption platform; coverage expanded to flexible workers; provincial-level unified management; integration with other housing security systems
- **Fiscal support:** 2026 special bond quota expected at 4.8 trillion yuan; continued expansion of fiscal tools for housing inventory reduction and land reserve
- **Green finance:** Continued growth as world's largest green bond market; stronger ESG integration in real estate financing; transition finance expansion for high-carbon industries; green buildings becoming standard in financing eligibility
- **Capital markets:** Developer financing shifting toward asset-light models; increased use of REITs, ABS, CMBS; insurance and pension funds as major long-term capital sources for rental housing

You are a research supervisor. Your job is to conduct research by calling the "ConductResearch" tool. For context, today's date is Sun Aug 23, 2026.

<Task>
Your focus is to call the "ConductResearch" tool to conduct research against the overall research question passed in by the user. 
When you are completely satisfied with the research findings returned from the tool calls, then you should call the "ResearchComplete" tool to indicate that you are done with your research.
</Task>

<Available Tools>
You have access to three main tools:
1. **ConductResearch**: Delegate research tasks to specialized sub-agents
2. **ResearchComplete**: Indicate that research is complete
3. **think_tool**: For reflection and strategic planning during research

**CRITICAL: Use think_tool before calling ConductResearch to plan your approach, and after each ConductResearch to assess progress. Do not call think_tool with any other tools in parallel.**
</Available Tools>

<Instructions>
Think like a research manager with limited time and resources. Follow these steps:

1. **Read the question carefully** - What specific information does the user need?
2. **Decide how to delegate the research** - Carefully consider the question and decide how to delegate the research. Are there multiple independent directions that can be explored simultaneously?
3. **After each call to ConductResearch, pause and assess** - Do I have enough to answer? What's still missing?
</Instructions>

<Hard Limits>
**Task Delegation Budgets** (Prevent excessive delegation):
- **Bias towards single agent** - Use single agent for simplicity unless the user request has clear opportunity for parallelization
- **Stop when you can answer confidently** - Don't keep delegating research for perfection
- **Limit tool calls** - Always stop after 3 tool calls to ConductResearch and think_tool if you cannot find the right sources

**Maximum 3 parallel agents per iteration**
</Hard Limits>

<Show Your Thinking>
Before you call ConductResearch tool call, use think_tool to plan your approach:
- Can the task be broken down into smaller sub-tasks?

After each ConductResearch tool call, use think_tool to analyze the results:
- What key information did I find?
- What's missing?
- Do I have enough to answer the question comprehensively?
- Should I delegate more research or call ResearchComplete?
</Show Your Thinking>

<Scaling Rules>
**Simple fact-finding, lists, and rankings** can use a single sub-agent:
- *Example*: List the top 10 coffee shops in San Francisco → Use 1 sub-agent

**Comparisons presented in the user request** can use a sub-agent for each element of the comparison:
- *Example*: Compare OpenAI vs. Anthropic vs. DeepMind approaches to AI safety → Use 3 sub-agents
- Delegate clear, distinct, non-overlapping subtopics

**Important Reminders:**
- Each ConductResearch call spawns a dedicated research agent for that specific topic
- A separate agent will write the final report - you just need to gather information
- When calling ConductResearch, provide complete standalone instructions - sub-agents can't see other agents' work
- Do NOT use acronyms or abbreviations in your research questions, be very clear and specific
</Scaling Rules>

I am researching the driving forces behind the sustainable development of China's real estate industry, and specifically how national policy, funding/financing, and guidance/regulation over the next 10 years (i.e., from 2026 through 2035) will promote the orderly and healthy development of the industry.

Please research and provide a comprehensive analysis covering the following dimensions:

1. Key driving forces (动力) for the industry's sustainable development — including but not limited to urbanization trends, demographic changes (aging population), housing demand shifts, technological innovation (smart buildings, green building, prefabricated construction), ESG/environmental sustainability requirements, and the transition from a "high-speed growth" to a "high-quality development" (高质量发展) model.

2. National policy (政策) over the next 10 years — analyze the regulatory framework, including the "housing for living, not for speculation" (房住不炒) principle, the dual-track/two-tier housing system (商品房 + 保障性住房), property tax (房地产税) reform, and land policy adjustments. What specific policy levers will the central government use to guide orderly development?

3. Funding and financing (资金) — analyze monetary policy, credit/financing support for developers, real estate investment trust (REITs/公募REITs) deployment, housing provident fund reforms, and how capital flows will be channeled toward sustainable/high-quality projects.

4. Guidance and direction (导向) — analyze industrial restructuring, consolidation of developers, shifting business models (from development-heavy to asset-light/operations-heavy), rental housing and affordable housing programs, and the role of local governments.

The research should cover the current situation as of 2026 and project forward to 2035. Where specific official targets, plans, or "15th Five-Year Plan"-related or longer-term strategies are available, please draw on them.

Preferred sources: Prioritize official Chinese government sources (e.g., 住房和城乡建设部, 中国人民银行, 国务院 policy documents, 国家发展和改革委员会), official policy documents and white papers, and reputable financial/industry analysis. Since the query is in Chinese, please prioritize Chinese-language authoritative sources (including official government websites and authoritative Chinese financial media such as 新华社, 人民日报, 财经).

Please synthesize the findings into a coherent explanation of what drives sustainable real estate development and how policy, funding, and guidance will jointly promote ordered, healthy industry growth over the next decade.

args.research_topic: Research the key driving forces (动力) behind the sustainable development of China's real estate industry over the next 10 years (2026 through 2035). Cover the following specific drivers in depth: (a) urbanization trends — including the projected pace of urbanization, new-type urbanization (新型城镇化) policy, urban renewal (城市更新), and the development of urban agglomerations and metropolitan areas; (b) demographic changes — aging population (人口老龄化), declining population growth, shrinking working-age population, and how these affect housing demand, particularly for elderly care housing (养老地产), and changes in household structure; (c) housing demand shifts — from first-home demand to improvement/upgrade demand (改善性需求), the end of the era of mass housing shortage, and the concept of a "housing demand floor"; (d) technological innovation — smart buildings (智慧建筑), green building (绿色建筑), prefabricated/assembled construction (装配式建筑), building information modeling, and digitalization of the industry; (e) ESG and environmental sustainability requirements — carbon peaking and carbon neutrality (双碳) goals for the construction and building sector, green building standards and energy efficiency targets; (f) the transition from "high-speed growth" to "high-quality development" (高质量发展) model. For each driver, find quantitative data (e.g., urbanization rate levels and projections, elderly population share, green building floor area targets) and official policy references where possible. Presents current situation as of 2026 and projections to 2035, drawing on official sources such as 国家发展和改革委员会 (NDRC), 住房和城乡建设部 (MOHURD), 国务院 policy documents, the "14th Five-Year Plan" (十四五规划) and any published content on the "15th Five-Year Plan" (十五五规划) research/drafting, 新华社, 人民日报, 中国新闻社. Use Chinese-language authoritative sources. The deliverable: a detailed written synthesis in Chinese-friendly but English-readable format, organized by driver, with data points, official target numbers, and forward-looking analysis.

Research the national policy (政策) framework and regulatory levers the Chinese central government will use over the next 10 years (2026-2035) to guide the orderly and healthy development of the real estate industry. Cover in depth: (a) the "housing for living, not for speculation" (房子是用来住的、不是用来炒的 / 房住不炒) principle — its status as a long-term guideline and how it is being operationalized; (b) the dual-track / two-tier housing system (双轨制：商品房 + 保障性住房) — including the 保障性住房 (affordable/safeguard housing) policies, 配售型保障性住房 (sale-type affordable housing) and 配租型保障性住房 (rental-type), large-scale construction plans announced around 2023-2024 (e.g., the 300万套 policy announced in 2024 by 中国人民银行 governor 潘功胜), and 城中村改造 (urban village renovation), 平急两用 (dual-use) facilities; (c) property tax (房地产税/房产税) reform — legislative status, pilot history (Shanghai and Chongqing), why rollout has been delayed, and prospects through 2035; (d) land policy adjustments (土地政策) — changes in land supply, 集中供地 (centralized land supply) policy changes, land price adjustment mechanisms, and turning land finance into a more sustainable model; (e) other regulatory levers — the "three red lines" (三道红线) for developer leverage and how they have evolved, mortgage lending policies (首付比例, 房贷利率), purchase restrictions (限购) and sales restrictions (限售) relaxation, 白名单 (whitelist) financing coordination mechanisms, and deleveraging vs. stabilizing policy balances; (f) any forward-looking policy directions from the 20th CPC Central Committee, Third Plenum decisions (二十届三中全会) of July 2024 (including the decision text on real estate), 中央经济工作会议 statements for 2024/2025/2026, and any published planning research for the "15th Five-Year Plan" (十五五规划, 2026-2030) and longer-term strategies to 2035 (including the 2035 vision from the 14th Five-Year Plan). Deliverable: a structured synthesis organized by policy lever, noting the timeline and evolution from current situation (as of 2026) to 2035, citing specific official document names, dates, and key phrases where possible. Prioritize Chinese-language official government sources: 住房和城乡建设部, 国务院, 中国人民银行, 国家发展和改革委员会, 新华社, 人民日报, 财经.

Research the funding and financing (资金) environment for China's real estate industry over the next 10 years (2026-2035) and how capital flows will be channeled toward sustainable and high-quality development. Cover in depth: (a) monetary policy — interest rate trends, 贷款市场报价利率 (LPR) trajectory, reserve requirement ratio (RRR) cuts, and the People's Bank of China (中国人民银行) stance on real estate financing; (b) credit and financing support for developers — the 白名单 (whitelist) financing coordination mechanism (城市房地产融资协调机制) launched in early 2024, loan amounts approved by late 2025, bank credit policies, and how these have shifted from the earlier 三道红线 (three red lines) deleveraging regime; (c) real estate investment trusts — 保障性租赁住房REITs and 公募REITs (public REITs) program expansion, types of underlying assets (e.g., affordable rental housing, commercial properties, 消费基础设施), how the REITs market supports the asset-light transition, and market size targets by 2035; (d) housing provident fund (住房公积金) reforms — policy rate changes, broader use of funds (e.g., for rental payments, second homes, supporting families having children), and possible prospect of transforming the provident fund system; (e) financing for specific segments — loans for urban village renovation (城中村改造), affordable housing (保障性住房), special bonds (专项债) support for land purchases and housing inventory reduction (收购存量商品房用作保障房 policy, 中国人民银行 300 billion yuan relending facility of 2024, and the 4 trillion yuan / one trillion yuan 特别国债 measures mentioned in late 2025 by 财政部); (f) indirect financing trends — capital markets, developer bond issuance, equity financing, and insurance/pension fund investment in rental housing; (g) how these financing tools will support sustainable/green projects (e.g., green bonds, 绿色信贷 for green buildings). Present the current situation as of 2026 (with the most recent data available, e.g., whitelist loan stats, REITs market scale, LPR levels from 2024-2025) and project forward to 2035. Cite specific official data points and policy documents. Prioritize Chinese-language authoritative sources: 中国人民银行, 国家金融监督管理总局, 证监会, 财政部, 新华社, 人民日报, 财经, and reputable financial analysis.

---

**Fully Comprehensive Findings**

---

## DRIVER (a): Urbanization Trends — Including Projected Pace of Urbanization, New-Type Urbanization (新型城镇化) Policy, Urban Renewal (城市更新), and Development of Urban Agglomerations and Metropolitan Areas

### Current Urbanization Level (as of 2025–2026)

As of 2024, China's urbanization rate reached 67%, with approximately 940 million people living in urban areas (Source: Tsinghua University article, Source 2; Ni Hong in Qiushi, Source 13). By end-2025, the urbanization rate rose further to 67.89%, with urban resident population at 953.8 million, up 10.3 million from the previous year, while rural population fell to 451.09 million (Source: NBS 2025 population data, Source 1 in the second set). China's urban population grew from 172 million in 1978 to 940 million in 2024, moving over 10 million people to cities annually (Source 2).

### Deceleration of Urbanization Pace

China's urbanization has entered a deceleration period. Wei Houkai (魏后凯), academic member of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, presented data showing that the average annual increase in urbanization rate was: 1.44 percentage points during the 9th Five-Year Plan, 1.35 (10th), 1.39 (11th), 1.48 (12th), 1.31 (13th), and only 0.78 percentage points in the first four years of the 14th Five-Year Plan (2021–2024) (Source 1 from NDRC, Source 1 in first set). The 2011–2020 period saw annual growth of 1.39 percentage points, decelerating to 0.78 percentage points in 2021–2024 (Source 13, Ni Hong in Qiushi).

The July 2025 Central Urban Work Conference — the first in 10 years — declared that China's urbanization is transitioning from rapid growth to stable development, and urban development from large-scale expansion to stock quality improvement, with urban renewal as the key mechanism (Source 12, CRIC report; Source 13, Ni Hong).

### Urbanization Rate Projections to 2030 and 2035

Wei Houkai (CASS) predicts the urbanization rate will grow about 0.7 percentage points per year over the next five years, reaching 71.5% by 2030, 74.6% by 2035, and approaching 80% by 2050 (Source 1 from NDRC, Source 1; Source 2, Tsinghua University). He noted that rural labor transfer is trending "near-home" and "local" migration, with county seats becoming key destinations (Source 2).

The China Index Academy (中指研究院) projects the urbanization rate will reach about 71.2% by 2030, adding about 0.7 percentage points annually (Source 9, 中指研究院 "十五五" outlook report).

The 2016 academic paper in Acta Geographica Sinica (地理学报) projected the urbanization rate reaching 70.12% by 2030, with total population at 1.445 billion, urban population at 10.13 billion, and rural population at 4.32 billion (Source 3, Sun Dongqi et al.). Provincial projections by 2030: Shanghai (99.89%), Beijing (99.46%), over 90% in Shanghai, Beijing, Tianjin, Guangdong, Zhejiang, Jiangsu; east economic belt 84.99%, central 66.02%, west 56.04% (Source 3).

BOC International Securities (2022 report) projected the urbanization rate would reach 75.57% by 2035, with total population peaking at 1.423 billion in 2028 (Source 6, BOC International).

### New-Type Urbanization (新型城镇化) Policy

New-type urbanization is defined as a "people-centered urbanization with Chinese characteristics, characterized by urban-rural coordination, urban-rural integration, industry-city interaction, intensive/resource-efficient land use, ecological livability, and harmonious development" (Source 4, Baidu Baike). The core concept is "people's urbanization" (人的城镇化), with the key being improving urbanization quality (Source 4).

The 20th CPC Central Committee's Fourth Plenary Session adopted proposals emphasizing "people-centered new-type urbanization," including promoting the citizenization of rural migrant workers and implementing a system of registering household registration based on place of residence for basic public services (Source 2).

Wei Houkai emphasized that the essence of agricultural population urbanization is "joint construction and joint sharing" (共建共享), with the fundamental solution being the registration of household registration by place of residence to provide equalized basic public services. This approach was placed first in the "15th Five-Year Plan Recommendations" (《建议》) (Source 1). The gap between the registered-resident urbanization rate and the household-registration urbanization rate (the "two rates gap") widened by 1.1 points during the 13th Five-Year Plan but narrowed by 0.64 points in the first three years of the 14th Five-Year Plan (Source 1).

The 2026 State Council Government Work Report (March 5, 2026) proposed promoting new-type urbanization and regional coordinated development (Source 4, Baidu Baike). The 2025 State Council Government Work Report called for scientifically and orderly advancing citizenization of agricultural transfer population (Source 4).

Key policy timeline for new-type urbanization (Source 4, Baidu Baike):
- December 2013: Central Urbanization Work Conference
- March 2014: National New-type Urbanization Plan (2014–2020) first systematically proposed goals/tasks
- 2022: NDRC issued 2022 key tasks with counties as key carriers
- 2024: Urbanization rate of resident population reached 67.00%, up 0.84 percentage points year-on-year
- December 2025: State Council 17th special study session on "deeply advancing people-oriented new-type urbanization, building new pattern of urban-rural integrated development" — Li Qiang emphasized releasing huge domestic demand potential in urban-rural integration

### Urban Renewal (城市更新) — The "15th Five-Year" Urban Renewal Plan

On May 22, 2026, the State Council issued the "Urban Renewal 15th Five-Year Plan" (国发〔2026〕12号), China's first national-level top-level design for urban renewal (Source 14, State Council Gazette; Source 4, Sina Finance; Source 2, Xinhua; Source 3, Xinhua Client; Source 4, Baidu Baike on urban renewal plan).

**Two-phase goals**: By 2030, urban renewal actions should achieve important progress with initial transformation of urban development/construction methods. By 2035, an innovative, livable, beautiful, resilient, civilized, and smart modern people's city should be basically built (Source 14; Source 4, Baidu Baike).

**Quantitative targets by 2030** (Source 14; Source 1, Sina Finance; Source 2, Xinhua; Source 4, Baidu Baike):
- Renovate approximately 500,000 sets of dilapidated urban housing (城镇危旧房)
- Start renovation of approximately 115,000 old residential communities (城镇老旧小区)
- Approximately 4,000 urban village (城中村) renovations
- Approximately 1,500 old street/factory area upgrades
- 128,000 hectares of new/expanded sports facilities
- 20,000 hectares of urban park green space improvements
- 365,000 km of underground pipeline renovation (gas, water supply, drainage, heating)
- 50,000 existing emergency shelters upgraded
- 95%+ digitalization of urban housing basic information

**Investment scale**: Multiple institutions estimate the total urban renewal market during the "15th Five-Year Plan" period at 15–20 trillion yuan (Source 1, Sina Finance, citing Zhang Wenzhong, Deputy Chairman of China Urban Planning Society: "market capacity estimated to exceed 15 trillion yuan"; Source 2, Xinhua; Source 4, Baidu Baike: "预计可完成投资15万亿元"). The underground pipeline segment alone covers ~600,000 km over five years with approximately 4–5 trillion yuan investment (Source 1, Sina Finance, citing Yan Yuejin). In 2024, approximately 2.9 trillion yuan was invested in urban renewal (Source 1).

**Financing mechanisms**: The plan supports local government special bonds, REITs and asset securitization, corporate bonds and medium-term notes, and establishes a shared funding mechanism among government, market, and residents based on the "who benefits, who contributes" principle (Source 2, Xinhua; Source 3, Xinhua Client). The NDRC arranged 97 billion yuan in central budget investment for urban renewal in 2026 and 160 billion yuan in ultra-long-term special treasury bonds for underground pipeline construction (Source 4, Baidu Baike).

**Key implementation dimensions** (Source 14):
- Building "good houses" (好房子) with quality housing projects, prefabricated decoration, elderly-adapted and barrier-free renovation
- Complete communities (15-minute living circles)
- Green low-carbon transformation (green buildings, ultra-low energy consumption buildings, carbon reduction, recycled materials)
- Urban safety and resilience (dangerous old housing renovation, seismic retrofitting, underground pipelines)
- Smart governance (CIM platform, digital transformation, blockchain for housing transactions)
- Policy innovations: transition periods of up to 5 years for revitalizing stock land, mixed land use, housing lifecycle safety management system (housing physical examination, safety funding, and quality safety insurance)

### Urban Agglomerations and Metropolitan Areas

China's 19 urban agglomerations carry over 70% of the population and contribute over 80% of GDP (Source 1, NDRC). Wei Houkai called for building a three-tier urban agglomeration system (world-class, national, and regional level). Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, Yangtze River Delta, and Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area should be positioned as world-class; the middle Yangtze River urban agglomeration could also qualify in the long term. The Chengdu-Chongqing economic circle should be included in national regional major strategies (Source 1).

With Shijiazhuang and Changchun metropolitan areas receiving NDRC approval in 2025, the number of national-level metropolitan areas has grown to 18 (Source 1).

The 15th Five-Year Plan Outline emphasizes consolidating Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, Yangtze River Delta, and Greater Bay Area roles, and advancing people-centered urbanization and new-type urbanization (Source 15, NDA summary of 15th Five-Year Plan draft).

---

## DRIVER (b): Demographic Changes — Aging Population, Declining Population Growth, Shrinking Working-Age Population, and Effects on Housing Demand

### Population Decline

China's population entered negative growth in 2022 for the first time since 1961, with a decline of 850,000 people (Source: Baidu Baike "人口负增长," Source 3 in second set; DW, Source 5 in second set). Official NBS data: 2022 births 9.56 million (birth rate 6.77‰), deaths 10.41 million (death rate 7.37‰), natural growth rate -0.60‰ (Source 3, Baidu Baike; Source 5, DW).

In 2023, the population decreased by 2.08 million, with a natural growth rate of -1.48‰ (Source 4, China Digital Space; Source 5, DW).

In 2024, the population declined by 1.39 million (Source 2, Zheng Bingwen in 求是网).

In 2025, the National Bureau of Statistics reported: end-2025 national population was 1,404.89 million (1.40489 billion), a decrease of 3.39 million from the end of the previous year. Births in 2025 were 7.92 million (birth rate 5.63‰), deaths 11.31 million (death rate 8.04‰), natural population growth rate -2.41‰ (Source 1, second set, NBS 2025 data).

The birth decline came much earlier and deeper than forecasts: China's Academy of Social Sciences had predicted 2027, the World Bank predicted 2029, and the Economist Intelligence Unit predicted 2025 peak (Source 8, BBC). The 2022 birth population (9.56 million) was lower than the number of university graduates that year (Source 4, China Digital Space).

### Aging Population Data

**Current status (end-2025)**: By end-2025, the 60+ population reached 323.38 million (23.0% of total population), and the 65+ population reached 223.65 million (15.9% of total population) (Source 1, second set, NBS 2025 data). China entered a moderately aging society in 2025 (Source 3, China.com.cn, "从养老到享老").

**Historical progression**: China crossed the aging threshold around 2000 when 65+ population reached 88.11 million (7.0%). By 2015, 65+ reached 144 million (10.5%). By 2021, 65+ population exceeded 200 million (14.2%), marking deep aging (Source 2, 求是网, Zheng Bingwen).

**Projections to 2035 and beyond**:
- He Dan and Liu Houlian (2019, Journal of the Party School of the CPC Central Committee): 65+ population projected to grow from 167 million (11.9%) in 2018 to 326 million (22.8%) by 2035 and exceed 400 million (29.3%) by 2050. Two elderly growth peaks occur in 2018–2022 and 2028–2039, with annual net increases of 8.6–11.2 million (Source 6, first set).
- NDRC Price and Cost Survey Center: 60+ population projected to exceed 300 million during the "14th Five-Year Plan" period (by 2025), reach 400 million by 2033, and peak at 487 million by 2053 (Source 7, first set, NDRC).
- UN forecasts: China will enter a "super-aging society" by 2032 when 65+ population reaches 278 million (over 20% of total) (Source 2, 求是网, Zheng Bingwen).
- World Bank (June 2024 China Economic Update): China became an "aged society" in 2023 with 15–20% of population aged 65+. Expected to reach ~28% in the next 20 years. Life expectancy rose from 60.2 (1974) to 78.2 years (2021); fertility fell from 4.2 children per woman to 1.1 (Source 10, first set, World Bank).
- BBC (2024): By 2050, each elderly person in China will have only 1.5 working-age people to support them (vs. 5 in 2020 and 2.4 in Britain). The 85+ population (oldest-old) will grow fastest, and by ~2050 China's oldest-old will exceed the total of the US and EU combined (Source 8, first set, BBC).

### Working-Age Population Decline

He Dan and Liu Houlian: The working-age population (15–64) will decline from 993 million in 2018 to 910 million by 2035 and 790 million by 2050 (Source 6, first set).

World Bank: The average labor force growth rate may decline from +0.3% (2000–2020) to -1.1% to -1.4% (2025–2045). Rising old-age dependency ratios are associated with lower total factor productivity. Female labor participation fell from 73% (1991) to 61% (2023) (Source 10, first set, World Bank).

By end-2025, the 16–59 years old population was 851.36 million (60.6% of total) (Source 1, second set, NBS 2025 data).

### Total Dependency Ratio

He Dan and Liu Houlian: Total dependency ratio will rise from 40.4 in 2018 to 58.4 (by roughly 2035) and then to 73 by 2050. China exits the demographic dividend window after 2030 (Source 6, first set).

Zheng Bingwen: Old-age dependency ratio (65+/15–64) rose from 10.1% (2001) to 22.8% (2024), projected to reach 33.7% (2035) and 52.3% (2050) (Source 2, 求是网).

NDRC (2022): By 2035, the elderly dependency ratio is projected to exceed 50%, meaning two young people will need to support one elderly person (Source 7, first set, NDRC).

### Population Projections

- He Dan and Liu Houlian: China's population will enter negative growth around 2029, peaking at 14.39 billion during 2020–2035, then declining to 13.7 billion by 2050 (Source 6, first set).
- Zheng Bingwen: Population projected to decline from 1.408 billion (2024) to 1.376 billion (2035) and 1.265 billion (2050) (Source 2, 求是网).
- Sina News (2024, citing State Council Development Research Center): Most institutions predict China's total population will be around 1.4 billion by 2035 and around 1.3 billion by 2050. Future annual births will drop by one million approximately every decade (Source 2, second set).
- World Bank: Total population expected to fall to 1.35 billion by 2045 (Source 10, first set).
- UN projections (via DW, 2023): China's population will decline by 109 million by 2050 — more than triple the UN's 2019 forecast (Source 5, second set).

### Effects on Housing Demand — Elderly Care Housing (养老地产) and Silver Economy

**Silver Economy Scale**: 
- As of end-2025, China's 60+ population reached 320 million (23.0% of total), marking entry into a moderately aging society (Source 3, China.com.cn, "从养老到享老").
- China's silver economy is currently estimated at approximately 7 trillion yuan (about 6% of GDP) (Source 3, China.com.cn).
- By 2035, the silver economy is projected to reach 30 trillion yuan, potentially accounting for 10% of GDP (Source 3, China.com.cn).
- The Fudan University Institute of Aging Research's "China Silver Economy Development Research Report" projects the silver economy will reach 19 trillion yuan by 2035, accounting for 28% of total consumption and 9.6% of GDP (Source 1, Xinhua, "银发经济" policy article).
- The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology reports China's elderly products market reached 5 trillion yuan in 2023 (Source 1, Xinhua).
- Elderly consumption potential is projected to grow to 106 trillion yuan by 2050 (Source 7, first set, NDRC).

**Institutional elderly care market**: As of end-2020, only 31 beds per 1,000 elderly people aged 60+. The "14th Five-Year Plan" targets 9 million beds by 2025. At 5,000 yuan/bed/month, the 2025 institutional care market is projected at 540 billion yuan (Source 7, first set, NDRC).

**Age-friendly renovation and smart homes**: About 40 million elderly fall at least once annually, about half at home. Nearly 60% of urban and rural elderly consider housing "not age-friendly." Retrofitting China's existing 40 billion sqm of old buildings for aging needs is estimated at 15 trillion yuan, with home renovation directly worth about 3 trillion yuan (Source 7, first set, NDRC).

**First "Silver Economy" policy document**: In January 2024, the State Council issued the "Opinions on Developing the Silver Economy and Enhancing the Welfare of the Elderly" (《关于发展银发经济增进老年人福祉的意见》), China's first-ever policy document dedicated to the silver economy, containing 26 measures (Source 1, Xinhua, "银发经济" policy article). The policy includes land use guarantees: new residential areas must allocate no less than 0.1 square meters per person for community elderly care facilities; counties with moderate or higher aging levels should raise this standard (Source 1, Xinhua).

**Policy framework milestones** (Source 2, 求是网, Zheng Bingwen):
- By 2025: Basic elderly care service system to be fully established covering all elderly
- By 2029: Elderly care service network basically complete
- By 2035: All elderly enjoy basic elderly care services
- 20+ provinces have issued local regulations on elderly care services

**Changing household structure**: The 2025 household size is approximately 2.42 persons, with family miniaturization bringing more housing demand (Source 6, 泽平宏观 "中国住房存量报告2026"). The empty-nest phenomenon is worsening: by late "14th Five-Year Plan," the "post-60s" generation will make up about 28% of the elderly. In 2020, empty-nest and solitary elderly reached 118 million. Family caregiving functions are weakening as children provide mostly financial support rather than physical care (Source 7, first set, NDRC).

**Pension fund pressures**: The CASS report "China Pension Actuarial Report 2019–2050" predicts pension income shortfall from 2028 and exhaustion of cumulative surplus by 2035 (Source 8, BBC; Source 10, first set, World Bank). Heilongjiang's pension funds were already depleted by 2016 (Source 8, BBC). The urban workers' basic pension insurance fund had a gap of 692.5 billion yuan in 2020 (income: 4,437.57 billion; expenditures: 5,130.14 billion) (Source 7, first set, NDRC).

## DRIVER (c): Housing Demand Shifts — From First-Home Demand to Improvement/Upgrade Demand, End of Mass Housing Shortage, and the Concept of a "Housing Demand Floor"

### The End of the Mass Housing Shortage Era

China's housing market has entered a new stage where supply-demand relations have fundamentally changed. As Minister Ni Hong stated: "At present, the people's housing needs have shifted from 'having or not having' (有没有) to 'good or not good' (好不好)" (Source 9, People's Daily; Source 14, Fujian MOHURD; Source 12, Xinhua "好房子").

As of 2025, China's urban housing is characterized by "total stock sufficient, structural imbalance" (总量够住、结构失衡) (Source 6, 泽平宏观 "中国住房存量报告2026"). The 2025 urban housing stock was 352.2 billion square meters, with urban per capita housing floor area of 37.0 square meters and approximately 3.77 billion housing units. The urban housing unit-to-household ratio (套户比) was 1.07 (Source 6, 泽平宏观).

The era of mass housing shortage is definitively over. During the 14th Five-Year Plan, total new commercial housing sales reached approximately 5.8 billion sqm (down 25% from the 13th Five-Year Plan). 2025 full-year commercial housing transactions are estimated to fall to around 900 million sqm (equivalent to 2009 levels) (Source 12, CRIC report). The 2021 peak marked the simultaneous peak of national population and new home sales (Source 9, 中指研究院).

### Housing Demand Floor — Projections for 2026–2035

Multiple research institutions have modeled the "housing demand floor" — the level of annual new housing demand that will persist as improvement and replacement needs dominate:

**Beike Research Institute (2022)** (Source 7, second set; Source 10, second set): China will generate 201–247 billion sqm of new housing demand during 2021–2035 (neutral scenario: 222 billion sqm, annual average 14.8 billion sqm). By 2035, total demand falls to 13.3 billion sqm, declining 2.5% annually. The population support ratio peaked in 2010, leading housing demand into a long-term decline phase. Demand composition (2021–2035, neutral scenario): rigid demand from rural-urban migration totals ~39 billion sqm (18% of demand, falling to 11% by 2035); improvement demand totals ~120 billion sqm (54%, rising to 58% by 2035); demolition/renovation demand totals ~63 billion sqm (28%, rising to 31% by 2035). By 2035, improvement plus demolition demand account for ~90% of total.

**Tianfeng Securities (2022)** (Source 8, second set): New commercial housing demand will follow an "L-shaped" decline trend. Central values: ~11.3 billion sqm/year (2022–2025), ~9.6 billion sqm (2026–2030), ~8.7 billion sqm (2031–2035). By 2035 (neutral): rigid demand share falls from 29% (2022) to 17%; improvement demand rises from 33% to 39%; update demand falls then rises to 44%.

**BOC International Securities (2022)** (Source 6, second set): Total new real housing demand projected to average 9.97 billion sqm/year before 2035, with new real demand of 10.11, 9.63, and 9.66 billion sqm in 2022–2024 respectively. With new-home sales at ~70% of total sales, the estimated commercial residential sales center is 7.0 billion sqm/year. After 2035, demand will decline but remain above 6.5 billion sqm/year.

**CITIC Futures (2022)** (Source 11, second set): Estimated annual housing demand above 14 billion sqm during 2021–2035, potentially reaching 14.6 billion sqm+ in 2022–2023.

**China Index Academy (2025)** (Source 9, second set): 2026–2030 new residential sales expected at ~3.63 billion sqm total, averaging ~730 million sqm annually (7–8 billion sqm range). Total urban housing demand projected at ~4.98 billion sqm over five years: (1) New urban population growth ~36.5 million people → 1.61 billion sqm demand; (2) Improvement/upgrade demand from rising per-capita housing floor space (up 2.1 sqm to 45 sqm) → 2.03 billion sqm (~40% of total, the core engine); (3) Demolition/redevelopment demand → 1.34 billion sqm.

**泽平宏观 (2026)** (Source 6, second set): 2025–2035 housing demand total about 111.5 billion sqm, annual average about 10.1 billion sqm. By 2035: rigid demand 26.9%, improvement demand 42.7%, update demand 30.3%. Improvement demand is the largest support.

**Lian Ping (2025)** (Source 7, second set): "15th Five-Year" annual housing sales to fall ~25% to about 6 million sqm equivalent area, with total sales of 3.2–3.5 billion sqm for the period. Annual real estate investment ~8.3 trillion yuan, falling 4.5%/year. The home-buying-age population may decline by about 21 million people (share from 39.2% to 38%). However, improvement-demand groups (ages 35–64) will grow from 630 million to 660 million annually.

### Improvement Demand as the Dominant Driver

The shift from first-home (刚性) demand to improvement (改善性) demand is the defining structural change in China's housing market. Driving forces have shifted from population growth and first-time home buying to improvement demand and housing replacement; the "好房子" (good housing) construction and urban renewal are now the main supports for new home market scale (Source 12, CRIC report).

Per-capita housing floor area data: In 2021, China's urban per capita housing floor area was 31.1 sqm (usable area about 24.9 sqm), below developed countries which are generally above 30 sqm usable area (Source 6, second set, BOC International). By end-2024, urban per capita reached about 41 sqm with households owning over 1.1 units on average (Source 13, second set, SJTU Chen Jie). Per-capita urban/rural housing floor space grew from 22.77 sqm (2000) to 41.76 sqm (2020) (Source 13, second set, SJTU Chen Jie).

CITIC Futures projected per-capita housing floor area would increase 0.8 sqm annually from 39.8 sqm in 2019 to 53.3 sqm by 2035 (Source 11, second set). The China Index Academy projects per-capita area rising to 45 sqm by 2030 (Source 9, second set).

In 2025, 120–144 sqm units in 30 key cities rose to 30% of supply; large units (120+ sqm) became mainstream new housing (Source 8, second set, 财联社). In the first three quarters of 2025, 120–144 sqm units in 30 key cities rose to 30% of supply (Source 8, second set).

### Housing Composition and Market Structure

By 2035, second-hand home GMV is projected to approach 14 trillion yuan, accounting for 47% of total housing transaction value, roughly equal to new home transactions (Source 10, second set, Beike; Source 7, second set, Beike). The neutral scenario for 2021–2035 projects new home market annual transaction value of ~15 trillion yuan and second-hand home market of ~9 trillion yuan (Source 10, second set).

The 15th Five-Year Plan Outline establishes a "保障房+商品房" dual-track supply system, with the first explicit call for "city-specific increases in improved housing supply" (因城施策增加改善性住房供给) (Source 9, People's Daily; Source 8, 财联社).

### Urban Housing Stock and Vacancy

As of 2025, the urban housing stock was 352.2 billion sqm with 3.77 billion housing units. The housing unit-to-household ratio (套户比) was 1.07 nationally, with significant regional variation: East 1.03, Central 1.02, West 1.11, Northeast 1.31. Nine provinces (Guangdong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, etc.) have a ratio below 1.0 (supply shortage), while three provinces (Heilongjiang, Jilin, Qinghai) exceed 1.3 (supply surplus). Among 336 prefecture-level units, 105 cities have a ratio below 1.0, and 140 cities have a ratio above 1.1 (Source 6, 泽平宏观).

Urban housing inventory is at historical highs: unsold commercial housing stood at 760 million sqm as of June 2025, up 52% from end-2020, with a sales-to-inventory ratio of 7.7 (up 2.5x from 2.3) (Source 7, second set, Lian Ping).

## DRIVER (d): Technological Innovation — Smart Buildings, Green Building, Prefabricated/Assembled Construction, BIM, and Digitalization of the Industry

### Prefabricated Construction (装配式建筑)

**Current status and targets**: By end of 2020, prefabricated buildings made up 20.5% of new urban construction (Source 14, second set, MOHURD "十四五" green building plan). The "14th Five-Year Plan for Building Energy Conservation and Green Building Development" targets prefabricated buildings reaching 30% of new urban construction by 2025 (Source 14, second set). As of 2023, the national average reached 25% of new construction, with Hunan province at 35% (above the national average) and Xiangtan City at 37.2% in 2023 rising to 54.1% in H1 2024 (Source 12, second set, academic paper on Hunan).

Shanghai's achievements: By end of 2020, cumulative prefabricated building area at land transfer stage reached ~150 million sqm; new prefabricated building above-ground area in 2020 accounted for 91.7% of all new buildings (Source 8, second set, Shanghai "十四五" plan). By 2025, Shanghai aimed to make prefabricated building the main construction method with 100% full decoration for new public rental housing (Source 8, second set).

**State Council Carbon Peak Action Plan (2021)** (Source 11, second set; Source 13, second set): Requires vigorously developing prefabricated buildings, promoting steel structure housing, and promoting building material recycling. The plan established that by 2025, all new urban buildings must fully implement green building standards.

**15th Five-Year Plan context** (Source 6, second set, 中研普华 report): "During the 15th Five-Year period, prefabricated construction shifts from 'scale expansion' to 'quality leap,' becoming the core vehicle for MOHURD's 'Good Housing' initiative and the State Council's Urban Renewal 15th Five-Year Plan green low-carbon transition." The industry has extremely low concentration (PC prefab component segment CR3 below 3%), typical "big industry, small company" characteristics.

**Urban renewal market opportunity** (Source 9, second set, 科技日报): The "15th Five-Year" urban renewal plan explicitly calls for "developing intelligent construction," "promoting prefabricated renovation," "raising the application ratio of prefabricated renovation," and "steadily developing prefabricated buildings." The 15th Five-Year urban renewal implementation involves a huge scale of direct investment, potentially driving trillions of yuan in investment and consumption.

**Key cost and technical challenges**: Initial costs are 10–15% higher than traditional cast-in-place construction. Long-term benefits (30% lower operational energy, 25% lower maintenance costs) take 10–15 years to materialize (Source 12, second set, academic paper on Hunan). PC plants generally face transport radius limits (economic within 200 km), so regional placement matters more than national expansion (Source 6, second set).

### Intelligent Construction (智能建造) Policy Evolution

The six-year policy evolution (2020–2026) is mapped by 16 official documents (Source 10, second set, smartbuilding.org.cn):

**2020 — Foundation**: The 13-ministry "Opinions on Promoting Collaborative Development of Intelligent Construction and Building Industrialization" (July 2020) assigned cross-ministry responsibilities. The target: by 2025, forming a group of leading intelligent construction enterprises; by 2035, achieving world-leading competitiveness in "China Construction" core competencies (Source 7, second set, MOHURD/NDRC/13-department opinion).

**2022–2025 — Pilot Phase**: In October 2022, MOHURD designated 24 pilot cities for a 3-year pilot program. 506 key enterprises (214 national high-tech), 758 demonstration projects, 47 standards/quotas/guidelines, and 99 universities offering intelligent construction majors (5,539 students in 2023, up 55% YoY) (Source 10, second set).

**2024 — Deepening**: The "Digital Housing and Construction" plan (Feb 2024) integrated intelligent construction into the "Digital China" framework. The CPC Central Committee and State Council (Nov 2024) listed intelligent construction as one of 11 key tasks in the "resilient cities" initiative.

**2025 — Standardization**: The first dedicated technical standard — 《智能建造技术导则（试行）》 (Feb 2025) — covered five stages: digital survey, digital design, intelligent production, intelligent construction, and smart operation/maintenance. Top-rated pilot cities: Suzhou, Shenzhen, Beijing, Xiamen, Changsha, Taizhou, Qingdao, Wuhan (Source 10, second set).

**2026 — National Strategy**: In March 2026, "developing intelligent construction and cultivating a modern construction industry chain" was written into the Government Work Report, placed alongside "intelligent manufacturing" within the "new productive forces" framework (Source 10, second set).

### BIM (Building Information Modeling)

The 13-ministry 2020 opinion called for BIM full-process application across all fields (Source 7, second set; Source 10, second set). The "14th Five-Year Plan for Building Energy Conservation" promotes BIM forward design, component RFID tracking, and digital twins (Source 14, second set). The 15th Five-Year Plan Outline calls for BIM throughout the full lifecycle of buildings (Source 10, second set). The 2025 MOHURD "Opinions on Improving Housing Quality" (建标〔2026〕66号) promotes BIM technology throughout the full lifecycle (Source 15, second set).

### Digitalization of the Industry

The Urban Renewal "15th Five-Year" Plan targets 95%+ digitalization of urban housing basic information by 2030 (Source 14, first set; Source 4, Baidu Baike on urban renewal plan). It requires CIM (City Information Modeling) platform construction, digital transformation, and blockchain for housing transactions (Source 14, first set).

The 2025 MOHURD "Opinions on Improving Housing Quality" (Source 15, second set) requires: building smart community information platforms, promoting smart home products and digital household development, and establishing full-lifecycle building safety management mechanisms.

The 15th Five-Year Plan Outline (Source 15, first set, NDA summary) calls for: strengthening computing power, algorithms, and data supply; advancing the "AI+" action across industries; and creating a healthy digital development ecosystem.

## DRIVER (e): ESG and Environmental Sustainability Requirements — Carbon Peaking and Carbon Neutrality (双碳) Goals for the Construction and Building Sector, Green Building Standards, and Energy Efficiency Targets

### National Carbon Peak Targets

The State Council's "Action Plan for Carbon Dioxide Peaking Before 2030" (October 2021) establishes (Source 11, second set; Source 13, second set; Source 15, second set, China Energy Portal):

**14th Five-Year Plan targets (by 2025)**: Non-fossil energy consumption share ~20%; energy consumption per unit of GDP to fall 13.5% from 2020; CO2 emissions per unit of GDP to fall 18% from 2020.

**15th Five-Year Plan targets (by 2030)**: Non-fossil energy consumption share ~25%; CO2 emissions per unit of GDP to fall over 65% from 2005 levels; achieving the primary goal of peaking carbon emissions before 2030.

**Wind and solar target**: By 2030, combined wind and solar installed capacity should reach over 1.2 billion kW (12亿千瓦).

### Urban-Rural Construction Carbon Peak Actions (Key Sector-Specific Targets)

The "Urban-Rural Construction Carbon Peak" action includes four key tasks (Source 11, second set; Source 13, second set):

1. **Green-low-carbon transformation**: Promote green low-carbon building materials and construction methods; accelerate new building industrialization; vigorously develop prefabricated buildings; promote steel structure housing; promote building material recycling; establish a green-low-carbon-oriented urban-rural planning management mechanism; prohibit large-scale demolition and construction.

2. **Improve building energy efficiency**: By 2025, all new urban buildings must fully implement green building standards.

3. **Optimize building energy consumption structure**: By 2025, renewable energy substitution rate in urban buildings should reach 8%; 50% of new public institution buildings and new factory rooftop photovoltaic coverage should be achieved. Build "solar-storage-DC-flexible" (光储直柔) buildings.

4. **Low-carbon transformation in rural construction**: Promote green farmhouse construction and energy-saving retrofits.

### Green Building Development — 14th Five-Year Plan Targets

The "14th Five-Year Plan for Building Energy Conservation and Green Building Development" (MOHURD, March 2022) (Source 14, second set) establishes:

**Overall goal by 2025**: New urban buildings fully built as green buildings. Building energy consumption capped at 1.15 billion tons of standard coal equivalent; new residential building energy efficiency improved by 30%; new public building energy efficiency improved by 20%.

**Specific targets by 2025**:
- Complete energy-saving renovation of over 350 million sqm of existing buildings
- Build over 50 million sqm of ultra-low/near-zero energy buildings
- Prefabricated buildings reach 30% of new urban construction
- Add over 50 million kW of solar PV capacity
- Apply over 100 million sqm of geothermal building applications
- Urban building renewable energy replacement rate reaches 8%
- Electricity exceeds 55% of building energy consumption

**13th Five-Year Plan achievements** (by end of 2020): New green buildings accounted for 77% of annual new construction; cumulatively exceeded 6.6 billion sqm of green buildings and 23.8 billion sqm of energy-efficient buildings (over 63% of urban civil building area) (Source 14, second set).

### The 15th Five-Year Plan and Green Transformation

The 15th Five-Year Plan Outline (Source 15, first set, NDA summary) includes green development as a key pillar: achieving carbon peaking; improving environmental quality; enhancing ecosystem stability; forming green production and lifestyle.

The RICS analysis (April 2026) (Source 11, first set) notes that under the 15th Five-Year Plan: green building evolves from new supply to stock transformation, with carbon policy shifting from intensity-based targets to dual control of total emissions and intensity. Zero-carbon industrial parks and buildings are national priorities. Full lifecycle carbon management becomes an operational imperative (monitoring emissions across design/construction/operations, low-carbon materials, renewable energy, smart building solutions).

The 2025 MOHURD "Opinions on Improving Housing Quality" (建标〔2026〕66号, Dec 31, 2025) (Source 15, second set) requires: all new urban housing shall fully meet green building standards; increase the proportion of high-star-rated green buildings; promote building energy conservation and carbon reduction; establish building energy efficiency grading; and compile carbon emission statistical accounting standards.

### Building Sector Carbon Emissions

The China Building Energy Efficiency Association (中国建筑节能协会) data shows building sector carbon emissions account for about 22.1% of national energy consumption, and existing building low-carbon renovation is an important direction (Source 4, Baidu Baike on urban renewal plan). The World Bank (June 2024) noted that China's carbon emissions grew 2.2% y/y in Q1 2024 (below GDP growth) as property-related industrial emissions fell, though renewable energy utilization rates declined due to grid constraints (Source 10, first set).
