## DRIVER (f): The Transition from "High-Speed Growth" to "High-Quality Development" (高质量发展) Model

### The Strategic Shift

The 15th Five-Year Plan period marks a fundamental reorientation of China's real estate industry. The RICS article (April 29, 2026) (Source 11, first set) states: "The Plan clearly articulates a transition from 'scale expansion' to 'quality enhancement,' from factor-driven growth to innovation-led development, and from fragmented optimisation to systemic coordination." Notably, the Plan elevates real estate to the strategic priority of "ensuring and improving people's livelihoods" rather than embedding it in urbanization frameworks. A key policy change establishes that new construction land will in principle no longer be allocated for commercial real estate development, ending the land-driven expansion model and beginning a stock asset management era (Source 11, first set).

The CRIC analysis (February 2026) (Source 12, first set) observes: "The 20th Central Committee 4th Plenary Session marked the first time 'real estate' directly appeared in the communiqué, integrating 'high-quality real estate development' into the 'guaranteeing and improving people's livelihood' framework — a shift from previous plenary sessions."

### Historical Context: From "Three Highs" to "New Model"

The traditional real estate model was characterized by "three highs" (high debt, high leverage, high turnover) which collapsed after 2021. 2025 new housing sales equaled only half of 2020 levels (Source 13, second set, SJTU Chen Jie). The 2021 Central Economic Work Conference first proposed exploring a new development model to promote healthy, positive circulation in the property sector (Source 7, second set, Beike).

Minister Ni Hong (2025 National Housing and Urban-Rural Development Work Conference, Dec 22–23, 2025) (Source 12, second set, Fujian MOHURD; Source 15, Guangzhou): "Continue to strive, fully exert effort, achieve a good start for high-quality development of housing and urban-rural construction in the '15th Five-Year Plan' period." The report noted that the construction industry's added value maintained above 6.5% of GDP, consolidating its pillar industry status. In 2024, the real estate and construction industries combined accounted for 13% of GDP (Source 9, People's Daily; Source 14, Shanghai press conference).

### Core Elements of the "New Model"

The 15th Five-Year Plan Outline (Source 15, first set, NDA summary; Source 13, Lingchuan County; Source 9, People's Daily; Source 8, 财联社) establishes:

1. **New housing supply system**: "保障房+商品房" dual-track system. Optimize affordable housing supply for urban wage earners and families in difficulty; increase improvement housing supply tailored to local conditions (因城施策). The wording for affordable housing shifted from "effective increase" (十四五) to "optimize" (十五五).

2. **New basic systems**: Improve basic systems for commercial housing development, financing, and sales. Implement a project company system and a main financing bank system for real estate development. Orderly advance presale-to-completed-construction (现房销售/现房销售) sales. Grant local governments greater autonomy for targeted regulation.

3. **"Good Housing" (好房子) construction**: Build "safe, comfortable, green, and smart" housing. The concept of "good housing" is defined by the "five pillars": good standards, good design, good materials, good construction, and good operations/maintenance (好标准、好设计、好材料、好建造、好运维) (Source 12, Xinhua "好房子").

4. **Full lifecycle housing safety management**: Establish housing physical examination, safety funding, and quality safety insurance systems.

5. **"People, housing, land, and capital" linkage mechanism**: Coordinating land supply with population dynamics and inventory.

### The "Good Housing" (好房子) National Standard

The new national "Residential Project Specification" (《住宅项目规范》) took effect on May 1, 2025, with 14 key improvements (Source 12, Xinhua; Source 14, Changzhi Housing Provident Fund; Source 13, SJTU Chen Jie):
- Minimum floor height raised from 2.8 meters to no less than 3.0 meters
- Elevator mandation raised from 7 floors to 4 floors and above
- Sound insulation improved: floor impact sound insulation performance improved from no more than 75 decibels to no more than 65 decibels

The MOHURD "Opinions on Improving Housing Quality" (建标〔2025〕66号, Dec 31, 2025) (Source 15, second set) sets the main goal: By 2030, significant progress in housing quality improvement — guaranteed/affordable housing becomes "good houses" first, commercial housing better meets rigid and improvement needs, and old houses see visible progress in renovation into "good houses."

Ni Hong (Minister of MOHURD) stated that through promoting good standards, design, materials, construction, and operations, "Good Housing" will be presented to consumers during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030) (Source 12, Xinhua "好房子").

### 14th Five-Year Plan Achievements and Baseline for the Transition

The 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021–2025) achievements (Source 15, Guangzhou; Source 14, Shanghai press conference; Source 12, Fujian MOHURD):
- Sold approximately 5 billion square meters of new commercial housing nationwide
- Built over 11 million units of various affordable housing and resettlement housing, benefiting over 30 million people
- Disbursed 6.5 trillion yuan in individual housing provident fund loans; supported withdrawal of 9.4 trillion yuan for housing consumption
- Renovated over 240,000 old residential communities, benefiting over 41 million households (110 million people)
- Installed 130,000 elevators; added 3.5 million parking spaces and 65,000 community service facilities
- Rebuilt 840,000 km of underground pipelines
- Created over 20,000 pocket parks and 27,000 km of urban greenways
- Construction industry total output reached 32.7 trillion yuan in 2024, with value-added of 9 trillion yuan

### The 15th Five-Year Plan Implementation Framework

The 15th Five-Year Plan Outline (March 2026) (Source 15, first set, NDA summary): The plan covers 2026–2030 and serves as the grand blueprint for building a modern socialist China. Key strategic areas directly relevant to real estate include: regional coordination (urbanization, city clusters), population strategy (fertility-friendly society, active aging response), people's livelihood (high-quality real estate development, social security, equalizing basic public services), green development (carbon peaking, green production and lifestyle), and risk prevention (coordinating orderly resolution of risks in real estate, local government debt, and small/medium financial institutions).

The 2026 Government Work Report explicitly called for: actively developing elderly human resources, formulating measures to promote high-quality development of the silver economy, and improving support policies for elderly products, pension finance, and relocation-based elderly care (旅居养老) (Source 3, China.com.cn).

### Expert Assessment of the Transition

Yang Fan (Zheshang Securities): "The real estate industry is expected to show signs of stabilization and repair in the mid-to-late Fifteenth Five-Year Plan period after bottoming out" (Source 8, second set, 财联社).

The CRIC analysis (Source 12, first set) concludes: Over the next five years, a people's livelihood orientation will run through the entire real estate development process; full-chain institutional reform in development, financing, and sales will deepen; presale-to-completed sales and pre-sales fund supervision will strengthen risk defenses; and factor marketization will accelerate revitalization of inefficient land and idle properties.

The RICS analysis (Source 11, first set) concludes: The Plan is a decisive turning point, redefining industry fundamentals through institutional, technological, and business model innovation. For industry participants it presents strategic opportunities to enhance operational capabilities; for society it promises improved housing quality, sustainable urban environments, and a more resilient housing system.

# Cleaned Research Findings: China's National Policy Framework for the Real Estate Industry (2026-2035)

---

## List of Queries and Tool Calls Made

1. "房住不炒 长期坚持 定位 政策 房地产新模式 2025"
2. "二十届三中全会 决定 房地产 租购并举 住房制度 原文"

15. "十四五规划纲要 2035年远景目标 住房 房地产 原文 全文"
16. "专项债 收储 闲置土地 收购存量商品房 2025 规模"
17. "城中村改造 平急两用公共基础设施 1万亿 2024 政策"
18. "潘功胜 保障性住房 再贷款 2024年9月 宣布 100% 比例"
19. "住房租赁条例 2025年5月 通过 国务院 公布"

---

## Fully Comprehensive Findings

### (a) The "Housing for Living, Not for Speculation" (房住不炒) Principle

#### 1. Origin and Status as a Long-Term Guideline

The principle "房子是用来住的、不是用来炒的" (houses are for living in, not for speculation) was first announced at the **December 2016 Central Economic Work Conference** and became the guiding principle for the housing market from the following year onward [Source 1]. 

The 2021 Central Economic Work Conference continued the "房住不炒" positioning from 2016, while promoting rental-purchase parity and long-term rental market development [Source 2]. The Xinhua News article (December 24, 2021) states: "坚持'房住不炒'定位不动摇" (Adhering unwaveringly to the "housing for living, not speculation" positioning) [Source 3].

At the July 2023 CPC Central Committee Political Bureau meeting, the phrase "房住不炒" was not mentioned, leading people to speculate that some restrictions might be relaxed. However, the State-run Economic Daily (《经济日报》) signaled in an editorial (August 23, 2023) that the "housing for living, not for speculation" positioning should still be upheld. The editorial stated that although the July Politburo meeting proposed "adapting to the new situation of major changes in the supply-demand relationship of the real estate market and timely adjusting and optimizing real estate policies," the "房住不炒" positioning should still be maintained and is not outdated. It is a general principle to promote the stable and healthy development of the real estate market and must be adhered to long-term [Source 1].

The editorial emphasized that in some hot cities, supply still falls short of demand, and if speculation returns, it could repeat the old path of over-reliance on real estate, which would harm economic and social development. The editorial noted that real estate-related loans account for 40% of bank credit, and 60% of Chinese residents' wealth is in housing, making it necessary to promote stable and healthy development of the market [Source 1].

#### 2. How the Principle Has Been Operationalized

Since the policy's implementation, market health in 38 major Chinese cities has improved compared to 2017, though 2018 saw a decline due to tightened regulation. Despite the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, most cities maintained health growth [Source 2].

**Key data points on operationalization:**
- Overall real estate demand is declining: In the first half of 2021, net real estate financing (including development loans, trusts, credit bonds, and USD bonds) was only ~100 billion yuan, down 87% from the same period in 2020 [Source 2].
- Starting July 2021, new home sales volume growth in major cities turned negative, with November 2021 down nearly 30% year-on-year [Source 2].
- Demographic drivers: Urban population growth slowed after 2016; new urban residents in 2020 decreased by 8.3 million from the 2016 peak. Marriage numbers in 2020 dropped 8.2 million from 2015. First-time homebuyers (ages 25-35) peaked in 2017 and are projected to decline 10% by 2025 and 20% by 2030 versus 2020 [Source 2].

The December 2021 Central Economic Work Conference noted China faces "threefold pressures" of demand contraction, supply shocks, and weakening expectations, reaffirming the "housing for living, not speculation" position [Source 2].

**2022 Market Adjustment Data (No "Hard Landing"):**
- Commercial housing prices fell 2.4% (first decline ever)
- Real estate development investment fell 10.0%; residential investment down 9.5%
- Start, construction, and completion areas down 7.2%, 39.4%, 15% respectively
- Sales area down 24.3%; residential sales area down 26.8%
- 2022 commercial housing sales area of 11.46 billion sq meters within predicted 10-12 billion range

[Source 5]

**Stakeholder Conditions:**
- 2019: 174 listed housing enterprises weighted average net debt ratio peaked at 91.37%
- Real estate loans ~40% of bank credit; 29% of loan balances; personal housing loans 54.35% of household loans
- Real estate industry debt = 60.09% of GDP (2019)
- 2017: household housing assets 77.7% of total assets; housing ownership rate 96.0%; 2018 urban household debt-to-income ratio 86.9%
- Land sales and real estate taxes = 33.94% of general public budget and government fund income (2019); 50% of local comprehensive financial resources (2020)

[Source 5]

**2023 Government Work Report (Premier Li Keqiang):**
"坚持房子是用来住的、不是用来炒的定位，建立实施房地产长效机制，扩大保障性住房供给，推进长租房市场建设，稳地价、稳房价、稳预期，因城施策促进房地产市场健康发展。" [Source 4]

**2024 Third Plenum Decision (July 2024):**
The 《中共中央关于进一步全面深化改革、推进中国式现代化的决定》 proposes building a "market + security" housing supply system and outlines four key areas for real estate reform. The Decision states: "加快建立租购并举的住房制度，加快构建房地产发展新模式。加大保障性住房建设和供给，满足工薪群体刚性住房需求。支持城乡居民多样化改善性住房需求。充分赋予各城市政府房地产市场调控自主权，因城施策，允许有关城市取消或调减住房限购政策、取消普通住宅和非普通住宅标准。改革房地产开发融资方式和商品房预售制度。完善房地产税收制度。" [Source 6]

**2025 Central Economic Work Conference (December 2025):**
The conference proposed "五个必须" (Five Musts) for 2026 economic work: fully tapping economic potential, combining policy support with reform and innovation, being both "dynamic" and "well-managed," combining investment in things and people, and coping with external challenges through internal strength [Source 10].

**2026 Government Work Report (March 2026):**
Compared to the 2025 report's emphasis on "continuing efforts to stop the decline and stabilize the market" (placed as the top priority in risk prevention), the 2026 report adopts the more measured language of "working to stabilize the real estate market" (着力稳定房地产市场). This wording change reflects a transition from emergency intervention to prevent rapid decline ("anti-stall") toward preventing volatility ("anti-fluctuation"), pursuing stable development on a healthier foundation [Source 18].

### (b) The Dual-Track / Two-Tier Housing System (双轨制：商品房 + 保障性住房)

#### 1. Historical Evolution of China's Housing Security System (Five Stages)

**Stage 1 (1993 and before):** Transition from welfare housing allocation (福利分房) to housing commercialization, initiated by Document No. 11 (国发〔1988〕11号) in 1988.

**Stage 2 (1994-2007):** Dual-track housing system established (1994), focusing on economically affordable housing (经济适用房) and low-rent housing (廉租房). Document 23 (国发〔1998〕23号) first proposed "廉租住房" (low-rent housing).

**Stage 3 (2008-2013):** Development of rental-type housing including public rental housing (公共租赁住房). From 2014, public rental and low-rent housing were merged and collectively called public rental housing.

**Stage 4 (2014-2018):** Shantytown renovation became the main focus; pilot programs for affordable joint-ownership housing (共有产权住房) began in 2014, with purchasers holding no less than 60% of property rights.

**Stage 5 (2019 onwards):** Formation of a system centered on public rental housing, government-subsidized rental housing (保障性租赁住房, with units under 70 sqm), and jointly-owned housing (共有产权住房).

[Source 14]

#### 2. Document No. 14 (14号文) — The New Housing Security System Framework

The "Guidance on Planning and Building Affordable Housing" (《指导意见》), passed August 25, 2023, establishes the core of a dual-track system separating affordable housing from commercial housing. Key requirements include:

**Adjustment of housing types:** Affordable housing divided into rental and sales types; new projects of talent housing and joint-ownership housing must be converted to sales-type affordable housing.

**Targets:** Focused on low-income working groups and introduced talent (scientists, teachers, medical staff); one unit per family.

**Planning:** Locally determined by city governments, combined with urban village renovation and urban renewal; based on demand.

**Land supply:** Allocated via 划拨 (allocated transfer) with only land costs paid; encouraged use of idle/inefficient industrial, commercial, or office land without paying land price differentials.

**Strict closed management:** "实行保障性住房严格封闭管理是《指导意见》确立保障房和商品房两套体系的重要措施。旨在严格保证保障性住房和商品房两套体系的独立性...禁止以任何方式违法违规将保障性住房变更为商品住房流入市场进行流通转让。" (Strict closed management is a key measure to ensure independence between the affordable and commercial housing systems, prohibiting any conversion of affordable housing into commercial housing for market circulation).

**Sales pricing:** Based on "保本微利" (cost-covering plus small profit) principle, covering allocated land costs and construction costs plus reasonable profit.

**Support policies:** Central subsidies, local government special bonds, development loans, individual housing loans, and pilot use of housing provident fund for development loans in cities with 3M+ urban residents.

[Source 14]

#### 3. The 300 Billion Yuan Reloan Facility (保障性住房再贷款)

**Announcement (May 17, 2024):** The People's Bank of China (PBOC) announced a 300 billion yuan (3000亿元) reloan facility for affordable housing at an interest rate of 1.75%, with a 1-year term renewable up to 4 times. It is distributed through 21 national banks including China Development Bank, policy banks, state-owned commercial banks, postal savings bank, and joint-stock commercial banks [Source 11].

**Mechanism:** PBOC Deputy Governor Tao Ling (陶玲) stated that banks lend under the principle of independent decision-making and self-risk bearing, with the PBOC providing reloans at 60% of loan principal, potentially driving 5,000 billion yuan (5000亿元) in bank loans. City governments select local state-owned enterprises as acquisition entities, with purchases strictly limited to completed, unsold commercial housing from real estate enterprises, treating enterprises of all ownership types equally [Source 11].

**Optimization (September 2024):** PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng (潘功胜) announced the PBOC's contribution ratio was raised from 60% to 100%, accelerating the destocking process. "为了进一步增强对银行、收购主体的市场化激励，我们将保障性住房再贷款政策中人民银行出资的比例，由原来的60%提高到100%。" [Source 11, Source 17]

**Implementation results:** Projects have been completed in multiple cities: Chongqing, Suzhou (Jiangsu), Wuhan (Hubei), Zhengzhou (Henan), Changchun (Jilin), Jinhua (Zhejiang), Baoding (Hebei), Leshan (Sichuan), Hefei (Anhui), Shucheng, and Mengcheng, with over 10,000 affordable housing units collected. Since November 2024, Hefei Anju Group acquired 5,733 units (589,000 sq meters) of existing commercial housing, serving tech enterprises, research institutes, and universities [Source 11].

#### 4. Large-Scale Construction Progress (2024 Data)

**2024 nationwide progress:** "今年以来，各地加大保障性住房建设和供给，建设筹集配售型保障性住房、保障性租赁住房、公租房共计172万套（间），一大批新市民、青年人、农民工住房问题得到解决。" (This year, all regions have increased construction and supply of security housing, building and raising a total of 1.72 million units of sale-type, rental-type, and public rental housing.) [Source 12]

**Three future priorities outlined by the Central Economic Work Conference:**
1. Planning - basing construction on actual demand (以需定建、以需定购), prioritizing locations with good transport and facilities for work-residence balance
2. Project construction - implementing fiscal, land, and financial support policies, accelerating construction and quality supervision
3. Setting "good housing" benchmarks - building model projects following "green, low-carbon, intelligent, safe" requirements

[Source 12]

#### 5. The Housing Rental Regulations (住房租赁条例)

**State Council Order No. 812:** Premier Li Qiang signed a State Council decree promulgating the "Housing Rental Regulations" (《住房租赁条例》), which will take effect on **September 15, 2025**. The regulations comprise 7 chapters and 50 articles [Source 21, Source 22, Source 23].

**Significance:** As China's first administrative regulation in the housing rental field, the Regulations mark the transition of the housing rental market from crude development to a legalized, standardized new stage and provide systematic institutional guarantees for addressing the "heavy purchase, light rental" problem and achieving the livelihood goal of "housing for all" [Source 9].

**Key provisions:**
- **Article 10:** Requires that deposit amounts, refund times, and deduction circumstances be specified in lease contracts, and prohibiting rental brokerage agencies and online platform operators from collecting or paying rent and deposits [Source 9].
- **Article 19:** Requires rental enterprises engaged in subletting to establish publicly disclosed housing rental fund supervision accounts, addressing "high-in-low-out" and "long-collection-short-payment" risks [Source 9].
- **Article 29:** Requires municipal-level governments to establish rent monitoring systems and periodically publish rent levels by region and housing type [Source 9].
- Non-residential spaces (kitchens, bathrooms, balconies, hallways, underground storage, garages) cannot be rented separately for residential purposes [Source 25].
- Real-name leasing contracts required, with mandatory filing through the housing rental management service platform (no fees charged for filing) [Source 25].

#### 6. Urban Village Renovation (城中村改造)

**2024 progress:** Urban village renovation expanded to over 300 cities, with 1,790 projects implemented [Source 15].

**2025 targets:** "2025年，为持续用力推动房地产市场止跌回稳，住房城乡建设部将加力实施城中村和危旧房改造，推进货币化安置，计划在新增100万套城中村改造和危旧房改造的基础上继续扩大改造规模。" [Source 15]

**Data:** "数据显示，仅在35个大城市，需要改造的城中村就有170万套。" [Source 15]

**Economic impact estimate:** Guosen Securities chief economist Xia Lei estimates that the 1 million-unit monetized resettlement could drive 200 million square meters of commercial housing sales, and reasonable land planning adjustments could drive approximately 500 billion yuan in on-site construction investment [Source 15].

**"一项目两方案" requirement:** Zhejiang University of Technology expert Yu Xiaofen notes the requirement for "一项目两方案" (one project, two plans) — each project must have complete compensation and funding balance plans before implementation to avoid new local government debt risks [Source 15].

**Three categories of renovation:**
- **Category 1:** Demolition and new construction (拆除新建)
- **Category 2:** Regular renovation/upgrading (整治提升)
- **Category 3:** Combination of both (拆整结合)

[Source 22, Source 23]

**Chongqing case study:** Chongqing has roughly 400 urban villages needing renovation. About 82 projects received national first-batch special loan support. On January 30, 2024, Chongqing's first urban village renovation special loan landed in the Wuyi Huzhu area of Dadukou District. Project total investment ~2.619 billion yuan, including 2.09 billion yuan in special loans [Source 23].

**Special loans:** By early June 2024, China Development Bank and Agricultural Development Bank of China had issued over 180 billion yuan in special loans for urban village renovation [Source 23].

#### 7. "平急两用" (Dual-Use) Public Infrastructure

**Definition:** "平急两用"公共基础设施建设是指在公共基础设施建设中，将平时使用和应急使用有机结合，打造一个既具备日常运营功能，又具备应急响应能力的基础设施系统，是集隔离、应急医疗和物资保障为一体的重要应急保障设施。 [Source 21]

**Policy timeline:**
- **2021:** Central Committee/State Council "Chengdu-Chongqing Economic Circle Plan" first proposed improving "平急转换" (peacetime-emergency conversion) capability
- **April 2023:** NDRC site meeting and Central Politburo meeting formally proposed the "平急两用" concept for super-large/extra-large cities
- **July 14, 2023:** State Council executive meeting approved the "Guiding Opinions on Actively and Steadily Promoting Public Infrastructure Construction for '平急两用' in Super-large and Extra-large Cities"
- **July 24, 2023:** Central Politburo meeting emphasized expanding affordable housing and promoting urban village renovation and "平急两用" infrastructure
- **December 2023:** Central Economic Work Conference listed the "Three Major Projects" as key measures to prevent and resolve risks in 2024

[Source 21]

**Scope:** Originally targeted at super-large cities (1000万+ population: Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, Chongqing, Guangzhou, Chengdu, Tianjin) and extra-large cities (500万-1000万). However, no policy prohibits other cities — e.g., Quanzhou (only 100-300万 population) was included in the first batch list with 60 projects totaling 30.117 billion yuan in investment [Source 21].

**Pinggu District (Beijing) case study — National pioneer:**
Five application scenarios: (1) 京平 Integrated Logistics Hub as suburban large warehouse for emergency material supply; (2) New rural community model (first in China at Nanshan Village); (3) Rural leisure complexes ("horizontal five-star hotels"); (4) 承平 Expressway Jinhai Lake service area with "交旅融合" (transport-tourism integration); (5) Jinhai Lake core area for rural revitalization [Source 21].

#### 8. The "Three Major Projects" (三大工程) — Overall Framework

The "three major projects" are: (1) accelerating affordable/subsidized housing construction (保障性住房建设), (2) building "dual-use" public infrastructure that serves ordinary purposes in peacetime and emergency functions in times of crisis ("平急两用" 公共基础设施建设), and (3) urban village renovation (城中村改造). These were designated as a major strategic deployment by the Party Central Committee and a key task for the current period [Source 22].

**Economic impact:** National Bureau of Statistics data shows the "Three Major Projects" contributed 0.6 percentage points to real estate development investment growth in Q1 2024 [Source 15].

**PSL funding:** On April 18, 2024, the People's Bank of China announced that the 500 billion yuan PSL (mortgage supplementary lending) allocated for the "Three Major Projects" had been fully disbursed in Q1 2024 [Source 11].

### (c) Property Tax (房地产税/房产税) Reform

#### 1. Legislative Status and Historical Background

**Distinction between 房产税 and 房地产税:**
- 房产税 (property tax) — a tax on properties, as piloted in Shanghai and Chongqing from 2011
- 房地产税 (real estate tax) — a comprehensive concept covering all taxes directly related to real estate economic activity, including business tax, corporate income tax, personal income tax, property tax, urban land use tax, city real estate tax, stamp duty, land value-added tax, deed tax, and farmland occupation tax

[Source 17]

**Historical timeline:**
- **1951:** State Council issued *Urban Real Estate Tax Interim Regulations* (combining real estate and land tax under then-existing land ownership)
- **1986 (Sept 15):** State Council issued the *Real Estate Tax Interim Regulations*, the first authorized legislation on real estate tax under public land ownership, establishing the "separation of land and property taxes" approach. Tax exemptions applied to personal non-commercial housing
- **2009:** State Council decided to launch real estate tax pilot reforms
- **2011:** Chongqing and Shanghai launched real estate tax pilot reforms — the first time the tax applied to individual non-operating housing (a "ice-breaking" moment)
- **2013:** The Third Plenary Session of the 18th CPC Central Committee called for "accelerating real estate tax legislation and advancing reform at the appropriate time" (law-led reform)
- **October 23, 2021:** The 31st Session of the Standing Committee of the 13th National People's Congress passed the "Decision on Authorizing the State Council to Conduct Real Estate Tax Reform Pilot Work in Certain Regions"
- **December 27, 2021:** The 2021 National Financial Work Conference called to "advance fiscal and tax system reform and prepare well for real estate tax pilot work"

[Source 19, Source 20]

#### 2. Shanghai and Chongqing Pilot Results

**Shanghai:**
- Scope:全市行政区域
- Reference price: "新房成交均价" for Shanghai's previous year
- Taxable objects: Local residents' new second+ homes, non-local residents' new homes
- Exemption: 60 sqm per capita
- Rates: 0.4% (if below 2x average) and 0.6% (if above 2x average)
- Tax base: 70% of transaction price
- 2020 revenue: 19.9 billion yuan (3.4% of total tax revenue)

**Chongqing:**
- Scope: 9 main urban districts
- Reference price: Average of previous two years' new home prices
- Taxable objects: Individually-owned standalone villas, newly purchased high-end housing (priced at 2x+ average), and "three-nothing persons" (no household registration, no enterprise, no job) purchasing 2nd+ ordinary homes
- Exemption: 180 sqm (pre-pilot villas), 100 sqm (post-pilot new villas and high-end housing)
- Rates: 0.5%, 1%, and 1.2% (three tiers)
- 2020 revenue: 7.2 billion yuan (5% of total tax revenue)
- Revenue used for: Public rental housing construction and maintenance

[Source 18, Source 20]

**Assessment of pilot results:**
- Both cities used area-based divisions and "old houses old rules, new houses new rules" policies
- Effects were limited: little impact on housing prices, small contribution to local fiscal revenue, and limited population coverage [Source 17]
- "沪渝的房产税试点，除具有破冰意义之外，还可归纳出房产税的三大功能，即完善地方税制、组织财政收入、收入再分配。" [Source 19]
- "2012年全年上海住房房产税收入约为92.5亿元，占全年税收收入的1%不到。重庆市2011年共征收住房房产税近1亿元，占全年财政收入的0.5%不到。" [Source 19]

#### 3. Why Rollout Has Been Delayed

**Two prerequisites for implementation:**
1. A unified real estate registration system to determine the number and ownership of properties nationwide
2. Determining how to tax the "land" portion of real estate tax (since residents only have use rights, not ownership, over land)

[Source 17]

**Finance Minister Liu Kun's statement (December 2020):**
"按照'立法先行、充分授权、分步推进'的原则，积极稳妥推进房地产税立法和改革。" [Source 18]

**Liu Kun's statement in the draft decision explanation (October 2021):**
"由于房地产市场全国差异很大，实际情况十分复杂，房地产税立法工作需要循序渐进、稳妥推进" [Source 20]

**China Academy of Fiscal Sciences President Liu Shangxi:**
"房地产税的出台要特别审慎，要权衡各方面的因素。征收房地产税要'立法先行'，房地产税开征关键是看立法进度，不立法肯定没有办法开征。" [Source 18]

**Current status (as of 2024-2025):**
The 2024 Third Plenum Decision states: "完善房地产税收制度" (improve real estate tax systems). The CRIC analysis of the Decision noted: "我们认为，未来交易环节税收负担有望进一步减轻，比如减免契税、增值税、个税等以促进住房消费。而持有环节的房地产税，受困于房地产市场持续低迷，短期内扩大试点及立法工作暂时搁置，但中长期来看仍有推进必要。" [Source 6]

**Key defect identified in pilots:**
"重庆、上海房产税试点有一个重大缺陷，就是不区分产权人的支付能力。" (The Chongqing and Shanghai pilots had a major defect: they failed to distinguish taxpayers' payment capacity.) China's housing is multi-track (reform housing/房改房, affordable housing, capped-price housing, etc.), often held by low-income, older state-sector workers at far below market prices — taxation at market values could be catastrophic for them [Source 19].

#### 4. Prospects Through 2035

- **Short-term (2024-2026):** Sheltered due to real estate market downturn. The CRIC analysis states: "受困于房地产市场持续低迷，短期内扩大试点及立法工作暂时搁置" [Source 6].
- **Medium-to-long-term (2027-2035):** Still considered necessary for local public finance, land finance transformation, and common prosperity. The CRIC analysis continues: "但中长期来看仍有推进必要" [Source 6].
- The 2024 Third Plenum Decision calls for "完善房地产税收制度" [Source 6].
- Expert Li Bo (PKU) recommends: "Introduce property tax for long-term management — increase cost of holding excess housing assets; property tax would optimize household asset structure, boost consumption, lower prices, boost real economy; revenue could supplement local finances, fund affordable housing, and allow adjustment of other taxes; recommend tax deductions/exemptions for first homes or families under 60 sqm per capita; advance pilot programs steadily." [Source 4]

### (d) Land Policy Adjustments (土地政策)

#### 1. Centralized Land Supply (集中供地) Policy Changes

**Origin (2021):** The "two centralization" (两集中) policy was launched in early 2021 in 22 pilot cities, requiring no more than 3 land transfer announcements per year. This was nicknamed a shift from "retail to wholesale" (零售变批发) [Source 2].

**Key adjustment (December 2022 Notice):** The Ministry of Natural Resources issued a notice titled "Notice on Further Regulating the Disclosure of Residential Land Supply Information" (《关于进一步规范住宅用地供应信息公开工作的通知》). Key changes:

1. Cities and counties must publish detailed lists of land plots to be offered in batches based on annual land supply plans, with each disclosure covering a period of at least 3 months
2. For plots on the detailed list, cities may issue transfer announcements once or multiple times during the disclosed period — meaning centralized disclosure remains required, but centralized organization of land auctions is no longer mandatory
3. Annual land supply plans must now be compiled starting in Q4 of each year and publicly released by March 31 of the following year, calculating supplies based on the average transaction volume of the past 3 years (reduced from the previous 5-year basis)
4. Cities with long housing de-stocking cycles, high land auction failure rates, or insufficient market demand must control residential land supply
5. Cities where unsold/undeveloped land exceeds 5 times the average of the past 3 years' transactions must strictly compress or suspend land supply
6. The policy now covers ALL cities nationwide, expanding from the original 22 pilot cities

[Source 2, Source 12]

**Expert interpretation:**
"Li Yujia noted this adjustment is not a cancellation of centralized land supply but an upgrade from version 1.0 to version 2.0 — version 1.0 responded to developers leveraging and speculating on land, while version 2.0 addresses refined and transparent land supply." [Source 2]

**Ministry of Natural Resources clarification (Feb 3, 2023):**
"不是要取消集中供地制度，而是优化完善集中供地政策，更好发挥充分公开披露信息对于稳定和引导市场预期的积极作用。" [Source 11]

#### 2. Document No. 38 (March 2026) — The "15th Five-Year Plan" Land Policy Framework

On March 16, 2026, the Ministry of Natural Resources and the National Forestry and Grassland Administration jointly issued the "Notice on Further Improving the Guarantee of Natural Resource Elements" (《关于进一步做好自然资源要素保障的通知》). The notice contains 13 policy measures [Source 1].

**Two "hard red lines":**
1. **Incremental-stock linkage:** Annual new urban-rural construction land must generally not exceed the area of revitalized stock land ("盘活一亩才能新增一亩" — only one mu of new land for each mu of revitalized land)
2. **New construction land prioritization:** New construction land should prioritize major projects and people's livelihood development and, in principle, should not be used for for-profit real estate development

[Source 1, Source 3]

**Key clarification from officials:**
- **Kong Weidong** (Director, Natural Resources Development and Utilization Department): "新增建设用地原则上不用于经营性房地产开发，这不等于不供应房地产用地，而是要重点用好存量资源'精供优供'，因城施策把握好供地的节奏和时序，优先布局区位优越、配套完善的区域，促进企业'拿好地、建好房'" [Source 1, Source 3].
- **Liu Yan** (Director, Land and Space Use Control Department): Implementation of total quantity control on construction land scale over the planning period shifts from annual national plans and quota allocation to provincial government coordination within the plan, granting provinces greater autonomy [Source 1].
- **Exception:** Scattered lands in urban village renovation (corner, sandwich, and interleaved plots, generally not exceeding 10% of total project area) involving affordable housing, public utility outlets, and retail commerce related to livelihood security may be handled through new land approval and supply [Source 1].

**Expert assessment:**
"38号文是'十五五'土地与房地产政策的定调文件，标志着房地产市场从增量扩张时代进入存量盘活时代" — 戴德梁行 魏东 [Source 3].

**Market impact:** The policy is expected to accelerate idle land purchase pace by local governments. Under the "reduce volume, improve quality" tone, hot cities like Shanghai, Hangzhou, and Guangzhou continue issuing residential land at a certain frequency with relaxed floor-area ratio and building density constraints, reflecting a "few but fine" supply strategy [Source 4].

#### 3. Land Finance Transformation — Special Bonds for Land Acquisition (专项债收储)

**2025 data:** "2025年，自然资源部积极配合财政部，指导各地发行地方政府专项债券5400余亿元主要用于收储存量闲置土地" [Source 1].

**2025 nationwide data (per China Index Academy):** In 2025, 26 provinces disclosed plans to use local government special bonds to repurchase idle land, with planned purchases exceeding 750 billion yuan, involving over 5,500 parcels and nearly 300 million sq meters. Over 300 billion yuan in bonds were actually issued. At an average floor area ratio of 2, this could remove ~600 million sq meters of potential inventory [Source 6].

**2026 data (as of end of February 2026):** 28 provinces/cities have disclosed planned special bond use for purchasing idle stock land totaling over 770 billion yuan, with actual issuance exceeding 335 billion yuan (~43%) [Source 4].

**Challenges identified ("三难"):**
1. **Price determination:** Governments typically base prices on the lower of historical cost or market appraisal, then add further discounts (often 70-90% of original sale price), leading sellers to resist
2. **Mortgage release:** Most developers have pledged land to financial institutions (often at ~60% of value), and repurchase prices below this require developers to repay loans out of pocket, hindering private enterprises (over 80% of proposed acquisitions are local state-owned enterprises)
3. **Future land use:** Unclear reuse plans risk re-idling and zoning changes face complex procedures

[Source 10]

#### 4. "标准地" (Standard Land) Transfer and Other Reforms

- Equal treatment of all economic ownership forms in land supply
- Prohibition of discriminatory bidding conditions (based on ownership type, location, equity structure, or brand)
- Support for "Standard Land" (标准地) transfer under the principle of "supply land, start construction immediately"
- Diversification of industrial land supply through long-term leasing, lease-then-transfer, and flexible term transfer

[Source 15]

### (e) Other Regulatory Levers

#### 1. The "Three Red Lines" (三道红线) for Developer Leverage

**Origin (August 2020):** The "Three Red Lines" were established on August 20, 2020, by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development and the People's Bank of China to reduce real estate developers' debt levels. The rules required:
- Asset-liability ratio (excluding advance receipts) no higher than 70%
- Net debt ratio no higher than 100%
- Cash-to-short-term-debt ratio no lower than 1.0

[Source 22, Source 23]

**Implementation:** 12 pilot developers were initially required to report. Companies were categorized into four tiers: Red-Orange-Yellow-Green (红-橙-黄-绿). In 2021, the policy expanded to the entire industry [Source 23, Source 25].

**Consequences:** "2021年'三道红线'政策扩围至全行业，此后房企融资遇冷，流动性压力持续增加，部分房企出现了流动性问题，至2025年违约房企累计达到78家" [Source 23].

**Phasing out (2023-2026):**
- Beginning in early 2026, developers are no longer required by regulators to report "三道红线" indicators monthly; only certain distressed developers must periodically report core financial data to risk disposal teams in their headquarters' cities [Source 21].
- According to five developers and financial departments interviewed by 21st Century Business Herald (January 2026), reporting of the "Three Red Lines" was no longer mandatory after mid-2023 [Source 22].
- A large distressed real estate company representative stated: "我们大概在2025年底接到口头通知，从今年（2026年）开始我们公司不再需要每个月上报三道红线相关指标，之前每个月都要上报。" [Source 25]

**Expert analysis on phasing out:**
- **Liu Shui** (China Index Academy): "The Three Red Lines was only 'window guidance' (窗口指导). Companies no longer reporting monthly indicates the policy is no longer used as a window guidance tool. The policy's goal of restricting debt scale growth and preventing aggressive expansion has been achieved." [Source 25]
- **Li Yujia** (Guangdong Provincial Housing Policy Research Center): "Companies topping sales charts are mostly state-owned enterprises, central enterprises, and quality private firms focusing on key cities, improving single-project profitability, and shifting to low-leverage, refined asset management." [Source 25]

**Industry transformation:**
"房地产业也告别'高杠杆、高周转、高风险'的旧发展模式，进入'低负债、高质量、稳增长'的新阶段。" [Source 21]

**Data on deleveraging results:**
- Country Garden's total borrowing balance dropped to RMB 271.31 billion by end-2022 (down 14.7% year-on-year); its asset-liability ratio (excluding advance receipts) fell from 81% in mid-2020 to 69.4%; net debt ratio fell to 40% [Source 22].
- 50 listed real estate companies' total interest-bearing debt scale has been decreasing year by year since 2022, falling to 5.1816 trillion yuan by mid-2025 [Source 23].
- As of December 2025, 21 distressed developers completed or received approval for debt restructuring, resolving cumulative debt of RMB 1.2 trillion, involving total liabilities exceeding RMB 2 trillion [Source 21, Source 22].

#### 2. Mortgage Lending Policies (首付比例, 房贷利率)

**September 24, 2024 — Major easing announced by PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng:**

- **Down payment:** "全国层面的商业性个人住房贷款将不再区分首套房和二套房，最低首付比例统一为15%" [Source 13].
- **Existing mortgage rate cuts:** "将存量房贷利率降至新发放贷款利率的附近，我们预计平均下降幅度在0.5个百分点左右...这一项政策将惠及5000万户家庭，1.5亿人口，平均每年减少家庭的利息支出总数大概1500亿元左右。" [Source 13, Source 18]
- **Policy rate cut:** 7-day reverse repo rate cut by 0.2 pp from 1.7% to 1.5% [Source 13].
- **RRR cut:** 0.5 percentage points, releasing ~1 trillion yuan in long-term liquidity; potentially another 0.25-0.5 pp cut before year-end. Average RRR fell from 7% to ~6.6% [Source 13].
- **Extension of real estate policy documents:** "Financial 16 Articles" and operating property loans extended from end-2024 to end-2026 [Source 13].

**2025 developments:** The 2025 Government Work Report shifted monetary policy from "稳健" (prudent) to "适度宽松" (moderately loose), last seen in 2009-2010. Further RRR cuts and rate cuts were expected [Source 17].

**Shanghai (August 2025):** Commercial loan rates no longer distinguished between first and second homes, uniformly reduced to LPR minus 45 basis points (3.05%). With a loan of 2 million yuan for 30 years, monthly payment dropped from 8,926 yuan to 8,297 yuan, saving 629 yuan per month, and over 226,000 yuan in interest over 30 years [Source 17].

#### 3. Purchase Restrictions (限购) and Sales Restrictions (限售) Relaxation

**Timeline of relaxation:**

- **May 2024:** Hangzhou fully eliminated housing purchase restrictions [Source 16].
- **September 2024:** Guangzhou became the first first-tier city to fully exit purchase limits [Source 16].
- **October 2024:** Tianjin fully eliminated purchase, transfer, and price restrictions for new and second-hand homes, and removed the distinction between ordinary and non-ordinary housing standards [Source 16].
- **By December 31, 2024:** 40 key cities — only 4 retained purchase restrictions (Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Haikou). Sales restrictions remained in 6 cities (Beijing and Shanghai had the longest at 5 years). Only Beijing still set land price ceilings [Source 18].
- **August 2025 (Beijing):** Beijing's 5th ring road purchase restriction lifted — homes outside the 5th ring road no longer subject to purchase limits. Single adults allowed to purchase under residential family policies. Second-home provident fund loan maximum 1 million yuan, minimum down payment 30% [Source 17].
- **August 2025 (Shanghai):** Outside the outer ring road, no purchase limits. Single adults (including non-Shanghai residents with 1 year of tax/social security) eligible for residential family policies. Commercial loan rates unified [Source 17].
- **August 2025 (Suzhou):** Cancelled the 2-year resale restriction on newly built commercial housing within urban areas [Source 20].

**Expert assessment:**
"自9月底中央定调'促进房地产市场止跌回稳'以来，北上广深和多个二线城市已陆续调整甚至完全取消限购等行政限制性楼市政策。" [Source 16]

"上海易居房地产研究院副院长严跃进：'除了天津，近日海南多地也全面退出限购，这意味着2010年以来实施的限购政策已逐渐走向退出历史舞台的阶段。'" [Source 16]

**2024 policy data:** "纵观2024年，地方累计出台房地产调控政策754条，处于历史高位。其中，宽松性政策683条，占比超过90%...整体来看，当前房地产政策环境已处于历史最宽松区间。" [Source 18]

#### 4. The "Whitelist" (白名单) Financing Coordination Mechanism

**Origin (early 2024):** The urban real estate financing coordination mechanism was established to support qualified real estate projects [Source 24].

**Data (as of early March 2025):** The National Financial Regulatory Administration reported that over 6 trillion yuan in loans had been approved for "whitelist" real estate projects, involving more than 15 million housing units already delivered or under construction [Source 24].

**Data (as of end of "14th Five-Year Plan" period):** During the "14th Five-Year Plan" period, the urban real estate financing coordination mechanism pushed "white list" project loans beyond 7 trillion RMB, supporting delivery of nearly 20 million housing units [Source 21].

**Shandong Province case study:** "山东省已于3月中旬将全部存量合规项目纳入'白名单'管理，全省共计纳入项目820个、贷款余额1974亿元，总计发放融资3343亿元" [Source 24].

**Extension (2026):** Regulators issued guidance allowing projects on the real estate financing coordination mechanism's "white list" to extend loans by 5 years with their original lending banks under certain conditions [Source 22, Source 23].

**2026 Government Work Report:** "进一步发挥'白名单'制度作用" — further strengthening the whitelist system as a core mechanism for ensuring housing delivery and preventing debt default risk [Source 18].

**"Financing lead bank system" (融资主办银行制):** A key future financing change, where one bank or syndicate serves as the designated bank for a project, holding project funds and ensuring reasonable financing needs [Source 25].

#### 5. Deleveraging vs. Stabilizing Policy Balances

The transition from the "three red lines" era to the stabilization era reflects a deliberate policy balance:

- **2020-2023:** Deleveraging phase — "三道红线" restricted developer debt growth, leading to industry-wide deleveraging
- **2023-2024:** Initial stabilization — gradual relaxation of financing restrictions, optimization of "三道红线" indicators
- **2024-2026:** Active stabilization — "白名单" mechanism, rate cuts, purchase restriction relaxation, "止跌回稳" (stop decline and stabilize) as the central policy objective
- **2026 onwards:** Focus on preventing volatility ("防波动") rather than preventing rapid decline ("防失速")

[Source 18, Source 21, Source 22, Source 25]

**2026 outlook:** The 2026 policy engine focuses on "融资纾困" (financing relief) and "供给优化" (supply optimization) [Source 23].

### (f) Forward-Looking Policy Directions

#### 1. The 20th CPC Central Committee, Third Plenum (July 2024)

**Decision text on real estate (《中共中央关于进一步全面深化改革、推进中国式现代化的决定》):**

The Decision proposes building a "market + security" housing supply system and outlines four key areas for real estate reform:

1. **Housing:** Establish a rental-purchase parallel housing system and accelerate a new real estate development model. Increase construction and supply of affordable housing to meet rigid housing needs of salary-earning groups, while supporting diversified improvement housing needs for urban and rural residents. Give city governments full autonomy in real estate market regulation (因城施策), allowing cities to cancel or reduce home purchase restrictions and abolish the distinction between ordinary and non-ordinary residential standards. Reform real estate development financing methods and the commercial housing presale system, and improve real estate tax systems.

2. **Employment and Income:** Stabilize employment and income expectations is a prerequisite for releasing potential housing demand. Expand the middle-income group size.

3. **Population and Urbanization:** Promote new urbanization, reduce residents' child-rearing and elderly-care burdens to support major consumption like housing. Improve birth support policies, develop elderly care, and implement household registration reforms granting equal social security, housing, and education rights to relocated agricultural populations.

[Source 6]

**Key analytical points from the CRIC analysis:**
- Only 6 provinces/cities still enforce purchase restrictions; Tianjin and Hainan are likely to follow in lifting them, and Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen still have significant deregulation space
- In 2023, Shenzhen, Shanghai, and Beijing abolished total price limits for ordinary housing; standards may be further relaxed or eliminated to reduce transaction tax burdens
- Housing sales may gradually transition toward spot/current sale (现售), though the presale system won't fully exit short-term
- Transaction-stage taxes (deed, VAT, personal income tax) may be reduced; the property tax on holdings is shelved short-term but will advance long-term

[Source 6]

**Beijing Normal University Professor Wan Zhe's commentary:**
"从此次决定的字里行间中，不难看出中国房地产市场的重大转型以及未来发展路径。" [Source 7]

"The Decision states clearly that it will accelerate the establishment of a housing system combining renting and purchasing and accelerate the building of a new real estate development model." [Source 7]

"The 'high turnover, high leverage' caused by one-sidedly emphasizing 'high speed' is bound to bring 'high prices' and 'high risks.'" [Source 7]

"The current real estate market is undergoing deep adjustment, which is the inevitable result of economic laws and industry development trends." [Source 7]

#### 2. The 20th Central Committee's Fourth Plenum (October 2025) — "15th Five-Year Plan" Recommendations

On October 28, 2025, the "Recommendations of the CPC Central Committee on Formulating the 15th Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social Development" were released. The Recommendations propose "推动房地产高质量发展" (promote high-quality real estate development), "加快构建房地产发展新模式" (accelerate the construction of a new real estate development model), and "完善商品房开发、融资、销售等基础制度" (improve basic systems for commercial housing development, financing, and sales) [Source 1, Source 2].

**Expert commentary:**

- **Pu Zhan** (Deputy Director, Policy Research Center of MOHURD): Improving relevant basic systems and enhancing the allocation efficiency of the four types of element resources — "人、房、地、钱" (people, housing, land, and money) — is a key measure for realizing the new model [Source 1].

**The Recommendations also propose:**
- "优化保障性住房供给" (optimizing the supply of affordable housing)
- "因城施策增加改善性住房供给" (increasing the supply of improved housing by city-specific policies)
- "建设安全、舒适、绿色、智慧的'好房子'" (building safe, comfortable, green, and smart "good houses"), implementing housing quality improvement projects and property service quality improvement actions

# Research Report: China's Real Estate Financing Environment (2026-2035)

## List of Queries and Tool Calls Made

1. Search: 城市房地产融资协调机制 白名单 贷款 金额 2025 国家金融监督管理总局
2. Search: 中国人民银行 3000亿 保障性住房再贷款 收购存量商品房 2024 2025
3. Search: LPR 贷款市场报价利率 2025 最新 5年期 房贷利率
4. Search: 公募REITs 保障性租赁住房 市场规模 2025 证监会
5. Search: 住房公积金 利率 下调 2025 提取 租房 多子女 改革
6. Search: 专项债 收购存量商品房 土地储备 2025 财政部 规模
7. Search: 财政部 4万亿 特别国债 2025 房地产 收购存量房
8. Search: 城中村改造 专项借款 规模 2025 保障性住房 贷款
9. Search: 绿色建筑 绿色信贷 绿色债券 房地产 2025 央行 规模
10. Search: 财政部 2025年11月 新闻发布会 房地产 专项债 存量商品房 万亿 新闻
11. Search: 央行 下调 存款准备金率 2025 降准 次数 RRR 7天逆回购 利率
12. Search: 三道红线 取消 房地产融资 政策 转向 城市房地产融资协调机制 2024
13. Search: 保险资金 长租房 保障性租赁住房 投资 2025 金融监管总局 不动产
14. Search: 房地产企业 债券发行 融资 2025 民营房企 信用债 证监会 支持

---

## Fully Comprehensive Findings

### (a) Monetary Policy — Interest Rate Trends, LPR Trajectory, RRR Cuts, and PBOC Stance

#### Loan Prime Rate (LPR) Evolution

**Current LPR Levels (as of mid-2026):**
- 1-year LPR: 3.00% (unchanged since May 2025)
- 5-year-and-above LPR: 3.50% (unchanged since May 2025) [12][13][14]

As of May 20, 2025, the PBOC cut both the 1-year and 5-year-and-above LPR by 10 basis points, bringing the 1-year LPR to 3.0% and the 5-year-and-above LPR to 3.5% [12]. The Bank of China's official LPR page shows historical data including the latest reading as of July 20, 2026, with both rates at 3.00% and 3.50% respectively [13].

**Historical LPR Trajectory (5-year+):**
- Aug 2019 – Jan 2020: 4.80%–4.85%
- Feb–Mar 2020: 4.75%
- 2020–2021: 4.65%
- Jan–Jul 2022: 4.45%–4.60%
- May 2022 – May 2023: 4.30%
- Jun–Jul 2023: 4.20%
- Aug 2023 – Jan 2024: 4.20%
- Jan–Jun 2024: 3.95% (a 25bp cut in February 2024, the largest single reduction since the new LPR mechanism was established) [15]
- Jul–Sep 2024: 3.85%
- Jan 2024 – Apr 2025: 3.10%/3.60%
- May 2025 onward: 3.00%/3.50% [13]

The 5-year LPR averaged 4.20% from 2019 to 2026, reaching an all-time high of 4.85% in September 2019 and an all-time low of 3.50% in May 2025 [14]. According to Trading Economics' global macro models and analyst expectations, the 5-year LPR is expected to remain at 3.50% through the end of the quarter and around 2027 [14].

A 10bp LPR cut in May 2025 was triggered by the PBOC's reduction of the 7-day reverse repurchase policy rate from 1.5% to 1.4% on May 7, 2025, signaling the expected LPR reduction. Following the LPR cut, multiple banks (ICBC, Agricultural Bank of China, Bank of China, China Construction Bank, Bank of Communications, China Merchants Bank, and China Everbright Bank) lowered deposit rates, marking the seventh round of deposit rate cuts, with some 1-year rates falling below 1% [11].

For Beijing homeowners, the first-home commercial mortgage rate dropped to 3.05% (a record low) after the May 2025 LPR cut. Second-home rates in Beijing fell to 3.45% (inside the 5th Ring Road) and 3.25% (outside), also both record lows. Using an example of a 1 million yuan, 30-year, equal-principal-and-interest first-home loan, total repayment would decrease by 19,600 yuan (from 1.5471 million to 1.5275 million yuan), with monthly payments dropping by 54.32 yuan (from 4,297.37 to 4,243.05 yuan) [11].

Financial regulator data shows that in Q1 2025, real estate loan balances increased by over 750 billion yuan, with new personal housing loans recording the largest quarterly increase since 2022 [11].

#### Reserve Requirement Ratio (RRR) Cuts

**2024 RRR Cuts:**
- On February 5, 2024, the PBOC cut the RRR by 0.5 percentage points
- On September 27, 2024, the PBOC cut the RRR by another 0.5 percentage points
- These two cuts together released about 2 trillion yuan in total liquidity [6][8]

**2025 RRR Cut:**
- On May 15, 2025, the PBOC lowered the RRR for financial institutions by 0.5 percentage points (excluding institutions already at the 5% RRR), and cut the RRR for auto finance companies and financial leasing companies by 5 percentage points [6][7]
- This was expected to release approximately 1 trillion yuan in long-term liquidity into the market [6][7]
- The average overall RRR declined from 6.6% to 6.2% [6]
- The Chinese Academy of Sciences, China Galaxy Securities research predicted that the May 7 package of monetary policies "is not the peak of easing; over the next 1-2 quarters, further easing may include additional rate cuts and RRR cuts, new policy financial instruments, restarting PSL (pledged supplementary lending), and creating or optimizing structural monetary policy tools targeting technology, consumption, foreign trade, property, and stock markets" [6]

**Policy Rate Cut:**
- On September 27, 2024, the 7-day reverse repurchase (repo) operation rate was reduced from 1.70% to 1.50% (a 20 basis point cut) — the largest policy rate cut in nearly four years [8]
- On May 7, 2025, the policy rate was further reduced by 0.1 percentage points — the 7-day reverse repo rate from 1.5% to 1.4%, expected to drive LPR down by about 0.1 percentage points [10]

#### PBOC Stance on Real Estate Financing

The PBOC has maintained a clearly supportive stance. PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng stated that the May 2025 RRR cut "supports a moderately loose monetary policy, improving the structure of liquidity provision to the banking system, reducing bank liability costs, and enhancing stability" [6]. The PBOC's Q1 2025 monetary policy report states it "will continue implementing a moderately loose monetary policy, flexibly managing intensity and pace to keep liquidity ample" [6].

According to KPMG China Minsheng Bank's chief economist Wen Bin, "future policy will focus more on quality and structure rather than simple aggregate easing, requiring coordinated fiscal, monetary, industrial, employment, and social security policies" [6].

As of December 2025, the average new corporate loan and personal housing loan interest rates were both around 3.1%, down 2.5 and 2.6 percentage points respectively since the second half of 2018, according to PBOC Vice Governor Zou Lan [4].

### (b) Credit and Financing Support for Developers — The Whitelist Mechanism

#### Establishment and Evolution

The Urban Real Estate Financing Coordination Mechanism (城市房地产融资协调机制) was established in January 2024 when the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (MOHURD) and the National Financial Regulatory Administration (NFRA) issued the "Notice on Establishing Urban Real Estate Financing Coordination Mechanisms" to guide coordination mechanisms in all prefecture-level and above cities [5].

In October 2024, MOHURD and NFRA held a national meeting to push for "expansion and enhancement" of the mechanism, expanding "whitelist" coverage to ensure compliant real estate projects are included [5]. NFRA Deputy Director Xiao Yuanqi stated that "all real estate projects meeting 'whitelist' standards should be managed accordingly, achieving 'all eligible should be included' (应进尽进)" [4].

#### Loan Approval Data

**Progression of Whitelist Loan Approvals:**

| Date | Approved Amount | Housing Units Supported |
|------|----------------|------------------------|
| End of 2024 | Over 5 trillion yuan | 14 million homes (as of Jan 22, 2025) |
| Jan 22, 2025 | 5.6 trillion yuan | 14 million homes |
| Early March 2025 | Over 6 trillion yuan | Over 15 million homes |
| May 7, 2025 | 6.7 trillion yuan | Over 16 million homes |
| September 22, 2025 | Over 7 trillion yuan | Nearly 20 million homes |

**Detailed breakdown:**

- **End of 2024:** NFRA's 2025 regulatory work conference on January 12, 2025, noted that "whitelist" project approvals passed over 5 trillion yuan in 2024 [2].
- **January 22, 2025:** NFRA Deputy Director Xiao Yuanqi disclosed at a State Council Information Office press conference that loan approvals had increased by 570 billion yuan from end-2024, reaching 5.6 trillion yuan, supporting the construction and delivery of 14 million housing units [3].
- **May 7, 2025:** NFRA Director Li Yunze announced at a State Council Information Office press conference that "whitelist" loans had grown to 6.7 trillion yuan, supporting over 16 million housing units, "effectively protecting the legitimate rights and interests of home buyers" and providing "important support for the real estate market's stabilization and recovery (止跌回稳)" [1].
- **September 22, 2025:** Li Yunze announced that "whitelist" project loans have exceeded 7 trillion yuan, supporting the construction and delivery of nearly 20 million housing units [5].

#### Regional Implementation Examples

- **Shandong Province:** By mid-March 2025, all existing compliant projects were included in the whitelist, with 820 projects and loan balance of 197.4 billion yuan. The province now has 1,826 whitelist projects, with 155 problematic projects successfully repaired and 334.3 billion yuan in total financing disbursed [4].
- **Henan Province:** On April 28, 2025, the Henan Provincial Government issued "Several Policy Measures for Fighting the Second Quarter to Ensure Double Completion," proposing to strengthen real estate "white list" project loan disbursement [4]. On September 17, 2025, Henan's Implementation Plan required leveraging the urban real estate financing coordination mechanism to regularly promote "whitelist" project financing [5].
- **Qingdao:** A 6-department notice in early April 2025 proposed aiming for 200 billion yuan in total credit and 150 billion yuan in actual funds, with "应贷尽贷、应展尽展" (lend everything that should be lent, extend everything that should be extended) [4].

#### Expert Analysis

Yan Yuejin (严跃进), Deputy Director of Shanghai E-House Real Estate Research Institute, noted that the mechanism "guides funds to precisely support 'guaranteed housing delivery,' injecting liquidity into real estate projects to accelerate completion" [5].

Li Yujia (李宇嘉), Chief Researcher of Guangdong Housing Policy Research Center, stated the mechanism "established a new financing model centered on real estate projects (rather than enterprises) with closed-loop fund operations, focusing on the project's own ability to generate and balance cash flow—meeting both reasonable project financing needs and financial institutions' risk control needs" [5].

Chen Wenjing (陈文静), Policy Research Director at China Index Academy, stated that next steps should include "clarifying due diligence exemption for financial institutions, accelerating whitelist funds and loan disbursement to improve corporate capital positions" [4].

#### Transition from "Three Red Lines" to the Whitelist Mechanism

The "Three Red Lines" (三道红线) policy was introduced in August 2020 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development and the PBOC, initially for 12 pilot real estate companies. The three indicators were: (1) asset-liability ratio (excluding advance receipts) no higher than 70%; (2) net debt ratio no higher than 100%; (3) cash-to-short-term-debt ratio no lower than 1.0. Companies were categorized into Red-Orange-Yellow-Green tiers with thresholds on interest-bearing debt growth [11][12][13].

In 2021, the policy expanded to the entire industry, leading to a sharp contraction in real estate financing and increasing liquidity pressure, with 78 developers defaulting cumulatively by 2025 [12].

**Key turning point:** On September 29, 2021, the PBOC and the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission jointly held a real estate financial work symposium emphasizing "accurately grasping and implementing the real estate financial prudent management system," marking a shift in real estate financial work amid rising debt pressure, declining housing transactions, and the appearance of unfinished housing projects [11].

**Policy termination:** As of the end of 2025/early 2026, multiple real estate companies confirmed they were no longer required to report "Three Red Lines" indicators to regulators on a monthly basis. A large distressed real estate company representative stated that "around the end of 2025, relevant colleagues received verbal notice from relevant departments that starting in 2026, the company would no longer need to report Three Red Lines indicators monthly" [15]. However, distressed developers are still required to report financial indicators like asset-liability ratios to special task force groups [13][15].

**Expert analysis on the termination:**

- Yan Yuejin: "The overall expansion momentum of industry debt has been fundamentally curbed, and the financial structures of surviving quality real estate companies have been generally optimized. The 'de-leveraging test period' preset by the policy has been fulfilled" [11].
- Liu Shui (刘水), Research Director at China Index Academy: "After four years of deep adjustment, real estate companies have fundamentally changed their operating philosophy, abandoning debt-driven scale growth in favor of high-quality development" [11].
- Li Yujia: "Companies topping sales charts are mostly state-owned enterprises, central enterprises, and quality private firms focusing on key cities, improving single-project profitability, and shifting to low-leverage, refined asset management. The high-leverage, high-debt expansion model has receded" [15].

The transition from the "Three Red Lines" restrictive framework to the "whitelist" supportive mechanism represents a fundamental shift from "preventing overheating" to "risk prevention, ensuring delivery, and promoting stability" (防风险、保交付、促稳定) [11]. In 2026, financing efforts will emphasize support for housing consumption, development loans, ensuring home delivery, resolving existing debt, and urban village renovation [11].

**New policy:** In early 2026, regulators issued guidance allowing projects on the "whitelist" to extend loans by 5 years with their original lending banks under certain conditions [12][13].

**Debt restructuring progress:** As of end-2025, 21 distressed property companies completed debt restructuring or reorganization, reducing approximately 1.2 trillion yuan of debt (covering about 2 trillion yuan of total interest-bearing debt). Debt reduction ratios generally ranged between 40%-70% (offshore bond restructuring ratios commonly exceeded 50%) [23]. Key milestones include: Sunac completed domestic bond second restructuring; Jinke became the first large A-share listed real estate company to complete judicial reorganization; Country Garden reduced 66% of $17.7 billion offshore debt; CIFI achieved offshore debt reduction ratio of 67% [23].

### (c) Real Estate Investment Trusts — REITs Market

#### Current Market Size (as of end-2025/early 2026)

As of December 2025, China had 78 listed public REITs with a total scale of 210 billion yuan (RMB), ranking first in Asia and second globally in product count [16]. By July 2026, 86 public REITs had been listed [20].

**Annual Issuance History:**
- 2021: 11 products (36.413 billion yuan)
- 2022: 13 products (41.948 billion yuan)
- 2023: 5 products (17.092 billion yuan)
- 2024: 29 products (65.517 billion yuan) [17]
- 2025: 20 new products (47.335 billion yuan raised from new issues and 5 expansions) [18]

CITIC Construction Investment forecasted 85 listed public REITs with 245 billion yuan by end of 2025 [17].

#### Asset Type Expansion

**Current asset classes (as of early 2025):** Public REITs underlying assets cover ten major sectors: parks (industrial parks), consumption, transportation, energy, warehousing logistics, affordable rental housing, municipal facilities, data centers, ecological/environmental protection, and water conservancy [16].

**2025 Milestones — "First-of-its-kind" issuances:**
- First data center REIT (南方万国数据中心REIT)
- First urban renewal industrial park REIT (华夏金隅智造工场REIT)
- First foreign-invested consumer infrastructure REIT (华夏凯德商业REIT) [16]
- First municipal facility project REIT [17]

**Affordable Rental Housing REITs:** By December 2025, 8 affordable rental housing (保障性租赁住房) REITs had been issued, with average annualized dividend rates of 3%, achieving full "invest, finance, manage, exit" loops. Insurers and real estate private equity funds are the main investors [16]. As of February 2025, affordable rental housing REITs had 8 projects totaling 9.419 billion yuan [17].

**Commercial Real Estate REITs Pilot:**
On December 31, 2025, the CSRC officially issued the "Announcement on Launching Commercial Real Estate Investment Trust (REITs) Pilot" (八条公告), effective from that date, along with the "Notice on Promoting High-Quality Development of the REITs Market" [18]. This formally includes commercial real estate (shopping malls, office buildings, hotels) in the public REITs pilot program, marking a "full asset class" breakthrough [16].

The institutional framework is a "1+3+N" structure: 1 announcement, 1 notice, 2 work regulations, and N (17 supporting rules) from Shenzhen/Shanghai Stock Exchanges, CSDC, Securities Association of China, and Asset Management Association of China. Review authorities are only the CSRC and Shanghai/Shenzhen exchanges; the timeline from confirmation of acceptance to first feedback was shortened from 30 to 20 working days [18].

The Notice emphasizes "increasing high-quality REITs supply, equal treatment of enterprises of all ownership types, supporting private enterprises to unlock idle assets through REITs, and guiding long-term funds (insurance, social security, annuity funds) into the secondary market" [18].

By mid-2026, 4 commercial real estate REITs had been listed with combined fundraising exceeding 200 billion yuan, including 汇添富上海地产商业REIT (40.92 billion yuan), 中金唯品会, 国泰海通砂之船, and 中信建投首农食品集团 [20].

Shenwan Hongyuan bond chief analyst Huang Weiping noted that the commercial REITs launch "implements the 'fifteenth five-year plan' proposal of 'revitalizing stock and optimizing increment'" [18].

#### REITs Market Supporting the Asset-Light Transition

Hu Feng (胡峰), Managing Director of Cushman & Wakefield North China, stated this marks "a new phase in China's property financialization, providing standardized exit channels for stock assets and boosting value reshaping of commercial office and hotel markets" [16]. Multiple industry insiders noted that "by opening up the 'invest, finance, manage, exit' loop, commercial real estate REITs help promote consumption, adjust structure, and build a new real estate development model" [20].

The market is shifting from development-and-sales models toward competition in full-cycle capabilities ("invest, finance, manage, exit"), with professional services and value operations becoming increasingly important [16].

#### Market Size Targets by 2035

Experts predict the market could reach trillion-yuan scale in the future [20]. Tian Lihui (田利辉), Dean of Nankai University's Financial Development Research Institute, noted that "since 2024, the NDRC and CSRC have issued policies establishing normalized issuance mechanisms, simplifying review processes, and expanding assets to include pension, cultural tourism, and new energy sectors, creating a 'primary issuance + additional offering' dual-driver model" [17].

He stated that "further market growth requires simplifying issuance procedures, optimizing valuation and trading systems, increasing long-term capital participation, strengthening the additional offering mechanism, and deepening special legislation." Key recommendations include compressing compliance review times (currently issuance cycles exceed 10 months), developing REITs ETF/index futures derivatives, addressing the fact that social security and pension allocated funds account for under 25%, and promoting independent REITs taxation systems [17].

#### REITs Expansion (扩募) Mechanism

The CSRC supports expansion via asset purchase, growth, and mergers. Public REIT expansions can sell to both unspecified and specified (定向扩募) investors; specified expansion is limited to 35 investors per offering (Shanghai Stock Exchange rule), with pricing no lower than 90% of the average trading price in the 20 trading days before the pricing benchmark date. Purchased assets should ideally be the same or related property type with operational synergies [20].

Examples: 中金厦门安居REIT (listed August 2022, initial 13 billion yuan) completed expansion of over 7 billion yuan in June 2025 to purchase affordable rental housing in Xiamen. 中航京能国际能源REIT expanded over 29 billion yuan (renamed after adding hydropower assets to original PV assets) [20].

### (d) Housing Provident Fund (住房公积金) Reforms

#### System Scale

According to the National Housing Provident Fund 2024 Annual Report:
- 2024 deposits: 3.631783 trillion yuan (up 4.67% year-over-year)
- 5.29 million contributing units, 176.2875 million contributors (up 6.92% and 1.00% respectively)
- By end of 2024, cumulative contributions totaled 32.794135 trillion yuan, with a balance of 10.925279 trillion yuan (up 8.61%)
- Cumulative 49.9911 million individual housing loans totaling 16.490108 trillion yuan had been issued [1][4]
- In 2024, 81.2704 million people withdrew 2.765484 trillion yuan (up 4.11%), with 46.10% of contributors receiving housing consumption support [1]
- 2.3056 million housing loans totaling 1.304307 trillion yuan were issued [1]
- Rental support: 22.5744 million people withdrew 272.05 billion yuan for rental housing (up 22.28% and 33.93% respectively) [1]
- Home improvement: 65,300 contributors withdrew 2.043 billion yuan for elevator installation and housing renovation [1]

#### Policy Rate Changes

On May 17, 2024, the PBOC announced a 0.25 percentage point reduction in individual housing provident fund loan rates. Effective May 18, 2024, new rates were:
- First-home: 5 years or less: 2.35%; over 5 years: 2.85%
- Second-home: 5 years or less: no less than 2.775%; over 5 years: no less than 3.325% [3]

On January 1, 2025, existing HPF loans began a batch interest rate reduction (no application required from borrowers), implementing the May 2024 rate cut [3].

On May 7, 2025, the PBOC further cut HPF loan rates by 0.25 percentage points:
- First-home: 5 years or less: 2.1%; over 5 years: 2.6% [5][10]
- Second-home: 5 years or less: 2.525%; over 5 years: 3.075% [5]

The Beijing Housing Provident Fund Management Center calculated that a 1 million yuan, 30-year first-home loan with equal monthly principal and interest payments would see monthly payments reduced by 134.59 yuan after the 2024 rate cut [3]. For a 1.2 million yuan first-home loan over 30 years, total interest was about 586,600 yuan (monthly payment 4,963 yuan) before adjustment, and about 529,500 yuan (monthly payment 4,804 yuan) after the 2025 adjustment [5].

#### Broader Use of Funds

In 2025, local governments issued 305 HPF optimization policies, accounting for 65% of demand-side policies [2]. About 280 HPF loan optimization policies were issued nationwide, including raising loan limits, adjusting loan counts, optimizing "commercial-to-provident" conversions, and broadening withdrawal uses (e.g., first home down payments, property management fees, renovation costs, and housing taxes) [4].

**Specific reforms by city:**
- **Shanghai:** Raised loan limits to a maximum of 3.24 million yuan for multi-child families — the highest among first-tier cities [2]
- **Shenzhen:** Allows multi-child families to withdraw up to 100% of monthly contributions or actual rent [1]; adjusted loan limits for multi-child families [4]
- **Hangzhou:** Offers up to 1.95 million yuan in loans for talent home purchases [2]
- **Changchun:** Expanded extraction to property fees, repair funds, and deed taxes in early March 2026 [2]
- **Fuzhou:** Allows withdrawing funds to purchase parking garages/spaces in the same community [4]
- **Hainan:** Allows withdrawal for medical expenses of contributors, spouses, or minor children hospitalized for major illnesses [4]
- **Yancheng:** Supports HPF for property fees [2]
- **Lanzhou:** Expanding commercial-to-provident loan conversion [2]
- **Ma'anshan (Anhui):** Supports full monthly deposit withdrawal for rent [1]

The extraction structure is currently concentrated: ~65% for purchasing/building/renovating homes and repaying loans, 9.8% for rental housing, and under 1% for old community renovation [2].

#### Reform Directions

The December 2025 Central Economic Work Conference called for "deepening housing provident fund system reform and orderly promoting 'good housing' construction" [1]. The 2026 Government Work Report also explicitly called for "deepening housing provident fund system reform" — the first time the fund has been mentioned in the Government Work Report since 2015, an 11-year gap [2].

**Key reform directions identified by experts:**

Qin Hong (秦虹), Senior Researcher at Renmin University's National Academy of Development and Strategy, outlined six reform directions [1]:
1. **Redefine strategic positioning:** Shift from single home-purchase support to a comprehensive "rent, purchase, renovation, maintenance" full-lifecycle housing consumption mutual assistance platform ("十五五" period goal)
2. **Strengthen legal foundation:** Elevate the current Administrative Regulations on Housing Provident Fund to higher-level legislation; expand coverage to flexible workers, platform economy participants, and self-employed individuals with differentiated contribution rates, flexible payment schedules, "interruption-reconnection" mechanisms, and SME support incentives
3. **Optimize mechanism design:** Adjust contribution bases/ratios by regional development level; maintain low-interest loan policies for first-time home buyers; promote intergenerational support models, "commercial-to-HPF loan conversion" (商转公), and monthly rent extraction with direct rent payment (按月提取、直付房租)
4. **Professionalize housing consumption support:** Extend services to home renovation, aging-appropriate modification, old district renewal, elevator installation, and housing maintenance; integrate housing special maintenance funds and commercial housing pre-sale supervision into the platform
5. **Enlarge fund scale:** Invest surplus funds in treasury bonds, local government special bonds, policy financial bonds, and quality equity products; provide differentiated deposit interest rates for retirees and voluntary contributors; one-time subsidies for first-time flexible worker accounts
6. **Build modern governance system:** Explore provincial-level unified management (省级统筹), cross-regional fund coordination and transfer, integrated credit and operating loan services with commercial banks, connection with public rental housing (公租房) systems, and a national integrated information system

Yu Xiaofen (虞晓芬), President of the China Housing and Real Estate Research Institute at Zhejiang University of Technology, argues the reform should "elevate successful local experiences to the national level and expand usage to old residential community renovation and elevator installation, supporting a full life-cycle of housing consumption" [4].

Li Yujia (李宇嘉) suggests reforms across "contribution, withdrawal, and lending — expanding contribution groups, improving cross-regional transfer and lending efficiency, and using fund appreciation income to support affordable rental housing and dormitory construction for new citizens and flexible workers" [4].

Chen Wenjing (陈文静), Policy Research Director at China Index Academy, believes "provident fund loan rates still have room to decline, and expects continued increases in loan limits — especially for families with multiple children — to boost housing consumption" [4].

#### Coverage Expansion

Pilot programs for flexible employment workers expanded from 6 initial cities (2021) to 13 cities (2023), then to 36 cities with an additional 23 cities added in 2024. By end of 2024, over 1 million flexible workers had deposited into HPF, with 240,000 actually using it [1].

The extraction rate was 76.15%, yet only 46.10% of contributors actually extracted funds. The national individual housing loan rate was about 74%, well below the 85% warning line, and over half of the 32 provinces/regions have loan rates below the national average [2].
